courses.title: Dramatic Literature
courses.description: Introduction, through careful reading of selected plays, to some of the major forms of Western drama, from the earliest tragedies of ancient Greece to the contemporary American theater.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Introduction to Poetry
courses.description: Comparative study of poetry in a variety of lyric and other poetic forms from different historical periods and different linguistic, national, and cultural traditions.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Humans & the Natural World
courses.description: Changing relationship between humans and the natural environment in ancient and modern authors as Virgil, Li Po, Basho, Darwin, and Thoreau.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Literature of the Abnormal Psyche
courses.description: Representations of the human psyche in literature and other media (film, visual arts, music) spanning cultures and historical contexts. Depictions of abnormal psychological states, including madness, obsession, and self-fragmentation. Textual interpretation informed by psychological theories. Rhetorical persuasion and nuanced argumentation.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Animals in Literature
courses.description: Study of literary texts from various periods and cultures whose theme is the representation of animals.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Ethnic Minority Writers in World Literature
courses.description: Consideration of a broad range of writers who speak from an ethnic perspective different from the nominally or politically dominant culture of their respective countries and who explore the challenges faced by characters significantly affected by their ethnic minority status.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Literature of East Asia
courses.description: Introduction to representative masterpieces of East Asia with readings from such works as The Story of the Stone, The Peach Blossom Fan, T'ang and Sung poetry, classical Japanese poetry, drama, and travel diaries, and The Tale of Genji.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); Oral Skills (OL); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Literature of South Asia
courses.description: Introduction to representative masterpieces of South Asia with readings from such works as the Mahabharata and Ramayana, The Cloud Messenger, Shakuntala, The Little Clay Cart, and the stories and poems of both ancient and modern India and Southeast Asia.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); Oral Skills (OL); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Literatures of the Islamic World
courses.description: Introduction to classical Islamic culture through translations of literature primarily from Arabic and Persian, as well as other languages. Topics include the concept of the self, society and power, spirituality, the natural world, the cosmos, and the supernatural.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); Oral Skills (OL); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Lower Division Seminar
courses.description: Examination of a special topic in a small group setting.

courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Directed group study.

courses.title: Student Facilitated Course
courses.description: Student facilitated course intended primarily for lower division students.
courses.prerequisites: UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; consent of instructor.

courses.title: Special Study for Undergraduates
courses.description: Special study for undergraduates.

courses.title: World Cinema
courses.description: Comparative, cross-cultural study of a topic, theme, or movement in world cinema beyond the boundary of a single national tradition. Topics may include "postsocialist cinemas in East Europe and Asia," "cinema and globalization," and "popular Asian cinemas."
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR), upper division standing, or consent of instructor.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); Visual Literacy (VL); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Hong Kong Cinema
courses.description: Hong Kong cinema, its history, industry, styles, genres, directors, and stars. Special attention to its polyglot, multicultural, transnational, colonial, and postcolonial environment.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR), upper division standing, or consent of instructor.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); Visual Literacy (VL); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Japanese Cinema
courses.description: Introduction to Japanese cinema from early silent films to the present. Explores important directors, genres, stars, themes and techniques in relation to specific historical and cultural contexts. Lectures and readings in English. Films in Japanese with English subtitles.
courses.prerequisites: Consent of instructor, or upper-division standing.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); Visual Literacy (VL); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Writing Nature: 1750 to the Present
courses.description: Study of representations, descriptions, and discussions of humankind's problematical relationship with the non-human world in texts written in a variety of European and American traditions between 1750 and the present.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Women Writers
courses.description: Exploration of women's differing views of self and society as revealed in major works by female authors of various times and cultures. Readings, principally of fiction, will include such writers as Lady Murasaki, Mme de Lafayette, and Charlotte Bronte.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Gender & Interpretation in the Renaissance
courses.description: Critical analysis of Renaissance texts with primary focus on issues such as human dignity, education and gender politics; "high" and "low" culture and its relation to literary practices.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Shakespeare & the Classical World
courses.description: Shakespeare's representations of the classical world in the light of selected ancient texts and Renaissance conceptions of Antiquity, with special attention to the depiction of politics and history.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Thematic & Structural Study of Literature
courses.description: Interpretation of selected works illustrating the historical evolution of themes, as well as of formal and structural elements.

courses.title: Introduction to Critical Theoretical Approaches to Literature & Culture
courses.description: Introduction to critical theory and its use for interpreting literary texts, film, and media forms in global culture.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Critical Reading & Analysis
courses.description: Close reading of selected texts; scrutiny of very limited amount of material, with attention to the problems of texts in translation.

courses.title: The Grotesque
courses.description: Study of the "grotesque" in selected texts from the Renaissance to the 20th century, with attention to the "grotesque" as a means of social, cultural, and political commentary, as well as of aesthetic innovation.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Representations of the City
courses.description: Exploration of the representation of the city in major translated literary texts from a variety of literary traditions and periods. Emphasis on the diversity of urban experience in literature. Topics include public and private space, memory, and gender.
courses.activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s), Extensive Writing.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Myth in Literature
courses.description: Comparative study of different versions of one or more central myths, with attention to their cultural settings, artistic and literary forms of representation, as well as to their psychological dimensions.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Modern Jewish Writers
courses.description: Problems of the modern Jewish experience from the perspective of the writer's construction of the self in relation to the future and to the non-Jew. Draws upon Russian, German, Yiddish, and American traditions.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Mystical Literatures of South Asia & the Middle East
courses.description: Exploration of the comparative mystical literatures of major religious traditions, with a focus on those produced in South Asia and the Middle East, although including other traditions.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Colonial & Postcolonial Experience in Literature
courses.description: Literary introduction to the cultural issues of colonialism and postcolonialism through reading, discussing and writing on narratives which articulate diverse points of view.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Literature of the Americas
courses.description: Study of the various stylistic, historical, social and cultural factors that contribute to a hemispheric vision of American literature, encompassing works by Canadian, United States, Caribbean, Brazilian, and Spanish-American writers.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Literature of the Americas (Taught in Latin America)
courses.description: Various stylistic, historical, social, and cultural factors that contribute to a hemispheric vision of American literature, encompassing works by Canadian, United States, Caribbean, Brazilian, and Spanish-American writers.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.activities: Lecture/Discussion 6 hour(s), Term Paper, Fieldwork 6 hour(s).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); Visual Literacy (VL); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: The Forms of Asian Literature
courses.description: Introduction to distinctive Asian literary forms, such as haiku, noh, the Chinese novel and tale, through reading of major works. Comparison with Western genres and study of native and Western critical traditions.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: African Literature
courses.description: Colonial and post-colonial sub-Saharan African literature and the African oral traditions from which it emerged. Genres and themes of African literature from the 19th century to the present.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Classical Literatures of the Islamic World 600-1900
courses.description: Major texts from Arabic, Persian, Ottoman Turkish and Urdu literature with attention to historical and cross-cultural context. Includes epic, romance, various genres of lyric poetry, fairy tales, historical and religious stories, mystical and philosophical narratives, and essays.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); Oral Skills (OL); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: The Ramayana
courses.description: Exploration of the Indian epic, Ramayana, through the lens of literature, performance, and visual art. Emphasis on the text's diversity and its contemporary global relevance. Topics include Ramayanas in Southeast Asia, and in various South Asian diaspora communities.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: War & Peace in Literature
courses.description: Through study of a few major works from Western and non-Western literature, illuminates the way in which literature from antiquity to the present has dealt with the antinomy peace/war through the ages.
courses.prerequisites: COM 001 or COM 002 or COM 003; or consent of instructor.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: The Detective Story as Literature
courses.description: Study of the origins, literary and social background, development and implications of the literature of detection in a comparative context.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Women in Literature
courses.description: Portrayals of women in literature, comparing selected heroines who represent a particular theme, period, or genre. Texts range around the globe and from ancient to modern works, such as Lysistrata, Emma, Hedda Gabler, The Makioka Sisters, and Top Girls.
courses.prerequisites: COM 001,COM 002,COM 003, or COM 004 or the equivalent recommended.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: The Modern Novel
courses.description: The changing image of man and his world as seen in novels by such writers as Joyce, Proust, and Mann.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: The Modern Drama
courses.description: Readings in representative authors such as Ibsen, Strindberg, Chekhov, Pirandello and Brecht.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Tragedy
courses.description: Persistent and changing aspects of the tragic vision in literature from ancient times to the present.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Comedy
courses.description: Comic attitudes towards life in literary works of different ages.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Writing Love & War in South Asia
courses.description: Comparative study of the themes and motifs of love and war in the literature of South Asia. Includes a discussion of Sanskrit epics, classical erotic court poetry, medieval heroic poetry, mystical compositions and colonial and post-colonial fiction.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); Oral Skills (OL); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Biography & Autobiography
courses.description: Portrayals of a human life in biographies and/or autobiographies of different countries and ages.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: The European Middle Ages
courses.description: Medieval literary genres as the foundation for modern literary forms. Topics and themes as love, God, vision, nature, history and politics, and sign theory.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: The Renaissance
courses.description: Literature, new science, gender, politics, and exploration in European Renaissance. Readings in Petrarch, Machiavelli, Montaigne, Tasso, Ariosto, Stampa, Shakespeare, LabÃ© and Aphra Behn.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Baroque & Neoclassicism
courses.description: Readings in major authors such as CalderÃ³n, Corneille, Pascal, Racine, Milton, and Grimmelshausen, with consideration of the tension between the expansive energies of the "baroque" and the restraints of dogma and reason.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: The Enlightenment
courses.description: Enlightenment writers such as Swift, Voltaire, Sterne, Rousseau, Wollstonecraft, and Kant. Emphasis on the revolutionary impact of 18th-century philosophical ideas and literary forms on modern political, social, and aesthetic culture.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Caribbean Literatures
courses.description: Comparative approach to the multi-lingual, multi-cultural literatures of the Caribbean. Works from English, French, and Spanish speaking regions with special attention to problems of identity, diaspora and resistance, class, gender, race.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.creditLimitations: Not open to students who have completed COM 165S.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Caribbean Literatures
courses.description: Comparative approach to the multi-lingual, multi-cultural literatures of the Caribbean. Works from English, French, and Spanish speaking regions with special attention to problems of identity, diaspora and resistance, class, gender, race.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open to students who have completed COM 165.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Literatures of the Modern Middle East
courses.description: Major translated works in modern Middle Eastern and North African Literature, including Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, and Turkish. Social and historical formation, with topics such as conflict and coexistence, journeys, and displaced people, gender and family.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: The Epic
courses.description: Study of various forms of epic poetry in both the oral and literary traditions.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: The Novel
courses.description: The novel as global genre: picaresque, epistolary, Bildungsroman, historical novel, contemporary forms.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Comparative Study of Major Authors
courses.description: Pivotal works of artists in the Western mainstream, such as Dante, Shakespeare, Cervantes, Goethe, Tolstoi, Proust, and Joyce.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Romanticism
courses.description: Introduction to the Romantic movement with emphasis upon Romantic concepts of the self, irony, love, the imagination and artistic creativity, and the relationship of the individual to nature and society.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Realism & Naturalism
courses.description: Novels and plays by Dickens, Zola, Flaubert, Dreiser, Ibsen, and Strindberg investigate marriage & adultery, the city & its perils, the hardships of industrialization, the war between the sexes, the New Woman, and other 19th-century themes.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: The Avant-Garde
courses.description: Studies in movements such as surrealism, expressionism and the absurd.

courses.title: The Contemporary Novel
courses.description: Study of important novels from different parts of the world, including Asia, Africa, Latin America, Europe, and the United States, in the period from the Second World War to the present.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Partition Literature: South Asia
courses.description: An exploration of novels, short stories, plays, and films in translation and in English, produced about the Partition of India in 1947.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: A Story for a Life: The Arabian Nights
courses.description: In-depth exploration of The Arabian Nights, the best-known work of pre-modern Arabic literature and a major work of world literature. Analysis of the work in its historical context and in comparison to other frame tales in world literature.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Sakuntala: The Story of a Ring
courses.description: A comparative examination of the Indian story of Sakuntala in multiple genres, languages, and media from the c. 400 BCE to the contemporary century.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); Visual Literacy (VL); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Shahnameh: The Persian Book of Kings
courses.description: In-depth analysis of the Persian Book of Kings (Shahnameh) by Abu al-Qasim Ferdowsi (d. 1020 CE) in its historical context with a comparative perspective on the role of this work in Persian and world literature.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Selected Topics in Comparative Literature
courses.description: Study of a selected topic or topics appropriate to student and faculty interests and areas of specialization of the instructor.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR); at least one course in literature.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Selected Topics in Comparative Literature
courses.description: Study of selected topics appropriate to student and faculty interests and areas of specialization of the instructor.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR); at least one course in literature or consent of instructor.
courses.activities: Lecture/Discussion 6 hour(s), Extensive Writing, Fieldwork 6 hour(s).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Internship in Comparative Literature
courses.description: Internships in fields where students can practice their skills.
courses.prerequisites: Consent of instructor. Completion of 84 units.

courses.title: Special Study for Honors Students
courses.description: Guided research, under the direction of a faculty member approved by the Program Director, leading to a senior honors thesis on a comparative topic.
courses.prerequisites: Consent of instructor. Open only to majors of senior standing who qualify for Honors Program.

courses.title: Senior Seminar in Comparative Literature
courses.description: Advanced study of selected topics and texts in Comparative Literature, with explicit emphasis on the theoretical and interpretive approaches that define Comparative Literature as a discipline and distinguish it from other literary disciplines. Required for the major.
courses.prerequisites: Senior standing as a Comparative Literature major or minor or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Tutoring in Comparative Literature
courses.description: Tutoring in undergraduate courses including leadership in small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with current courses offered by Comparative Literature.
courses.prerequisites: Consent of instructor. Upper division standing with declared major in Comparative Literature.

courses.title: Directed Group Study for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.description: Directed group study.

courses.title: Student Facilitated Course
courses.description: Student facilitated course intended primarily for upper division students.
courses.prerequisites: UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; consent of instructor.

courses.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates.

courses.title: Topics & Themes in Comparative Literature
courses.description: Comparative, interpretive study of the treatment of specific topics and themes in literary works from various periods, societies, and cultures, in light of these works' historical and sociocultural contexts.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Comparative Literature, English, or a foreign-language literature, or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Approaches to Lyric Poetry
courses.description: Analysis and interpretation of poetic texts in different historical periods and national literatures, with consideration of major theoretical developments in the understanding of poetic discourse.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Forms of the Spiritual Quest
courses.description: An exploration, culminating in a research paper, of changing forms of the quest for transcendence in different cultures, mainly in major works of Western literature, but also in other traditions and from the perspectives of other disciplines.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor; knowledge of at least one foreign language.

courses.title: Literary Genres
courses.description: Comparative literature of major works in a particular genre from various linguistic, national, and cultural traditions, with particular attention to historical developments within the genre and to genre theory.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Comparative Literature, English, or a foreign-language literature or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Gender & Interpretation
courses.description: Study of how literary texts from different periods, societies, and cultures represent gender roles and gender hierarchy, building on recent work on gender in anthropology, literature, psychology, and women's studies.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Research in Primary Literature
courses.description: Individually guided research in the primary literature of concentration, under the supervision of a faculty member culminating in a conference paper. Required of M.A. and Ph.D. candidates.

courses.title: Research in Second Literature
courses.description: Individually guided research in the secondary literature of concentration, under the supervision of a faculty member, culminating in a paper. Required of Ph.D. candidates.

courses.title: Research in Third Literature or Special Topic
courses.description: Individually guided research, under the supervision of a faculty member, in the third literature of concentration or on a special topic culminating in a paper. Required of Ph.D. candidates.
courses.activities: Conference 1 hour(s), Term Paper, Independent Study 8 hour(s).

courses.title: Dissertation Prospectus
courses.description: Individually guided writing of the dissertation prospectus under supervision of a faculty member. Must be taken prior to completion of the qualifying exam. Required of Ph.D. candidates.

courses.title: Proseminar: Comparative Literature: Past, Present, Future
courses.description: History, theory, and methodology of comparative literature. Issues of national literature, world literature, and comparative literature. Relation of comparative literature to other disciplines and diverse expressions. Discussion of current problems in teaching and research in comparative literature. Required of M.A. and Ph.D. candidates.

courses.title: Contexts of the 19th-Century Novel
courses.description: Development in 19th-century history, culture, and society in relation to major trends in the 19th-century novel.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Directed Independent Study in Primary, Secondary, or Third Literature
courses.description: Directed Independent Study in Primary, Secondary, or Third Literature culminating in term paper. Only for languages with no graduate course offerings.
courses.activities: Conference 1 hour(s), Term Paper, Independent Study 8 hour(s).

courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Directed group study.

courses.title: Individual Study
courses.description: Individual study.

courses.title: Special Study for the Doctoral Dissertation
courses.description: Special study for the doctoral dissertation.

courses.title: Teaching Comparative Literature in College
courses.description: Discussion of the theory and practice of teaching composition at the college level in a department of comparative literature in relation to the major cultural and social developments and with specific application to the introductory COM 001,COM 002,COM 003,COM 004.
courses.prerequisites: Appointment as a Comparative Literature Associate Instructor or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Teaching Internship in Comparative Literature
courses.description: Regular consultations between the student instructor teaching Comparative Literature courses and a supervisor. Specifically designed for first-time TAs in COM 005,COM 006,COM 007, and COM 010. Instruction in the teaching of writing in a literature course, grading of papers, leading discussions.

courses.title: Teaching Assistant Training Practicum
courses.description: Teaching assistant training practicum.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence for All
courses.description: Comprehensive introduction to artificial intelligence (AI) and its multifaceted applications. Foundational understanding of modern AI to enable effective communication about its functions, recognition of its applications, and awareness of its core principles. Ethical and societal implications of AI.
courses.creditLimitations: No credit for students that have taken ECS 111,ECS 170,ECS 171,EEC 174AY,EEC 174BY,EEC 179, or BIM 155.

courses.title: Introduction to Media Computation
courses.description: Introduction to key computational ideas necessary to understand and produce digital media. Fundamentals of programming are covered as well as analysis of how media are represented and transmitted in digital form. Aimed primarily at non-computer science students.
courses.creditLimitations: Two units of credit for students that have taken ECS 010, ECS 030,ECS 032A,ECS 032AV,ECS 036A, or ENG 006..
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Science & Engineering (SE); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Data, Logic, & Computing
courses.description: Display, processing, and representation of information and data on a computer. Understanding and analyzing the digital representations of numbers, images, and sounds. Basic computer operations and their logic. Introduction to discrete mathematics in computer science, including propositional logic, proofs by induction, recursions, and counting. Introduction to algorithms. Uses of computers and their influence on society.
courses.prerequisites: MAT 016A (can be concurrent) or MAT 017A(can be concurrent) or MAT 019A{ can be concurrent } or MAT 021A(can be concurrent).
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed course ECS 020 or MAT108.

courses.title: Discrete Mathematics For Computer Science
courses.description: Discrete mathematics of particular utility to computer science. Proofs by induction. Propositional and first-order logic. Sets, functions, and relations. Big-O and related notations. Recursion and solutions of recurrence relations. Combinatorics. Probability on finite probability spaces. Graph theory.
courses.prerequisites: MAT 016A C- or better or MAT 017A C- or better or MAT 019A C- or better or MAT 021A C- or better.

courses.title: Introduction to Programming
courses.description: Introduction to programming and problem solving in Python. Aimed primarily at non-major students.
courses.creditLimitations: No credit to students who have completed ECS 032B,ECS 032C,ECS 036A,ECS 036B,ECS 036C.

courses.title: Introduction to Programming
courses.description: Introduction to programming and problem solving in Python. Aimed primarily at non-major students.
courses.activities: Web Virtual Lecture 3 hour(s), Web Electronic Discussion 1 hour(s).
courses.creditLimitations: No credit to students who have completed ECS 032B,ECS 032C,ECS 036A,ECS 036B,ECS 036C.

courses.title: Introduction to Data Structures
courses.description: Design and analysis of data structures using Python; trees, heaps, searching, sorting, and graphs.
courses.prerequisites: ECS 010 C- or better or ECS 030 C- or better or ECS 032A C- or better or ECS 032AVC- or better or ECS 036A C- or better.
courses.creditLimitations: No credit to students who have completed ECS 036B,ECS 036C, ECS 040 or ECS 060.

courses.title: Implementation of Data Structures in C
courses.description: Programming in the C language. Use of basic UNIX tools. Writing good programs of increased complexity and efficiency. Implementation of data structures in C.
courses.creditLimitations: No credit to students who have completed ECS 036B,ECS 036C, ECS 040 or ECS 060.

courses.title: Software Development in UNIX & C++
courses.description: UNIX Operating system tools and programming environment. Methods for debugging and verification. Principles object-oriented programming in C++.
courses.prerequisites: ECS 032C C- or better; or consent of instructor.
courses.creditLimitations: No credit to students who have completed ECS 036B,ECS 036C, ECS 040 or ECS 060.

courses.title: Programming & Problem Solving
courses.description: Computers and computer programming for students with some prior experience, algorithm design, and debugging. Good programming style. Use of basic UNIX tools.
courses.prerequisites: ECS 032A C- or better or ECS 032AVC- or better or ECS 010 C- or better; or must satisfy computer science placement exam; prior experience with basic programming concepts (variable, loops, conditional statements) required.
courses.creditLimitations: Only 2 units of credit to students who have completed ECS 032A or ECS 032AV; no credit to students who have completed ECS 032B,ECS 032C,ECS 034, ECS 040 or ECS 060.

courses.title: Software Development & Object-Oriented Programming in C++
courses.description: Object-oriented programming in C++. Basic data structures and their use. Writing good programs of increased complexity and efficiency. Methods for debugging and verification.
courses.prerequisites: ECS 030 C- or better or ECS 036A C- or better.
courses.creditLimitations: No credit to students who have completed ECS 032B,ECS 032C,ECS 034, ECS 040 or ECS 060.

courses.title: Data Structures, Algorithms, & Programming
courses.description: Design and analysis of data structures for a variety of applications; trees, heaps, searching, sorting, hashing, and graphs. Extensive programming.
courses.prerequisites: (ECS 040 C- or better or ECS 036B C- or better);ECS 020 C- or better.
courses.creditLimitations: No credit to students who have completed ECS 032B,ECS 032C,ECS 034, ECS 040 or ECS 060.

courses.title: Computer Organization & Machine-Dependent Programming
courses.description: Comparative study of different hardware architectures via programming in the assembly languages of various machines. Role of system software in producing an abstract machine. Introduction to I/O devices and programming.
courses.prerequisites: ECS 040 C- or better or ECS 036B C- or better or ECS 032C C- or better.
courses.creditLimitations: 1 unit of credit if student has taken EEC 070.

courses.title: Ethics of Technology
courses.description: Foundations of normative ethics for technology, its relationships to moral philosophy and to the law. Technologies and their impacts on the environment and society. Justice, meritocracy, and computer science and engineering. Ethical issues with AI and machine learning.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have taken ECS 188.

courses.title: Applied Machine Learning for Non-Majors
courses.description: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Course Description:Machine learning methods and their application. Theory, design and evaluation of supervised/unsupervised machine learning algorithms. Practical use of matching learning methods and their challenges.
courses.prerequisites: (ECS 032B or ECS 036C); (MAT 135A or STA 035C); (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067).
courses.creditLimitations: No credit if student has taken ECS 171; not intended for Computer Science and Computer Science Engineering Majors.

courses.title: Computer Security for Non-Majors
courses.description: Principles, mechanisms, implementation, and sound practices of computer security and data protection. Cryptography, authentication and access control. Internet security. Malicious software. Common vulnerabilities. Practical security in everyday life. Not intended for Computer Science or Computer Science & Engineering majors.
courses.prerequisites: ECS 010 or ECS 030 or ECS 032A or ECS 032AV or ECS 036A.
courses.creditLimitations: No credit allowed to students who have completed ECS 153 or ECS 155.

courses.title: Computer Networks for Non-Majors
courses.description: Overview of computer networks, World Wide Web, email, local & wide-area computer networks, TCP/IP protocol suite, network protocols for data transmission, introduction to network programming.
courses.creditLimitations: No credit for students who have completed any of ECS 152A,ECS 152B,ECS 152C,EEC 173A, or EEC 173B.

courses.title: Databases for Non-Majors
courses.description: Overview of Database Systems, Conceptual Modeling and Design, E/R diagrams, Relational Model, Relational Algebra, SQL, File and Index Structures, Query Evaluation, Transaction Concepts, Concurrency and Recovery, and NoSQL Databases.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit for students who have completed ECS 165A or ECS 165B.

courses.title: Algorithms for Data Science
courses.description: Algorithms for searching, pattern matching, combinatorial problems, clustering, and time series analysis with practical emphasis.
courses.creditLimitations: No credit if ECS 122A has been taken.

courses.title: Data Processing Pipelines
courses.description: Introduction to software systems for processing large datasets. Hands-on experience with scripting, data streams, distributed computing, and software development and deployment infrastructure.

courses.title: Theory of Computation
courses.description: Fundamental ideas in the theory of computation, including formal languages, computability and complexity. Reducibility among computational problems.

courses.title: Algorithm Design & Analysis
courses.description: Complexity of algorithms, bounds on complexity, analysis methods. Searching, sorting, pattern matching, graph algorithms. Algorithm design techniques: divide-conquer, greedy, dynamic programming. Approximation methods. NP-complete problems.

courses.title: Algorithm Design & Analysis
courses.description: Theory and practice of hard problems, and problems with complex algorithm solutions. NP-completeness, approximation algorithms, randomized algorithms, dynamic programming and branch and bound. Theoretical analysis, implementation and practical evaluations. Examples from parallel, string, graph, and geometric algorithms.

courses.title: Theory & Practice of Bioinformatics
courses.description: Fundamental biological, mathematical and algorithmic models underlying bioinformatics and systems biology; sequence analysis, database search, genome annotation, clustering and classification, functional gene networks, regulatory network inference, phylogenetic trees, applications of common bioinformatics tools in molecular biology and genetics.
courses.prerequisites: (ECS 032A or ECS 032AV or ECS 036A or ENG 006); (STA 032 or STA 035B or STA 100 or STA 131A or ECS 132 or MAT 135A or EEC 161 or BIM 105); (BIS 002A or MCB 010).

courses.title: Cryptography
courses.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of cryptographic techniques used in computer security. Encryption (secret-key and public-key), message authentication, digital signatures, entity authentication, key distribution, and other cryptographic protocols. The social context of cryptography.
courses.prerequisites: (ECS 020 or MAT 108); (ECS 010 or ECS 032A or ECS 032AV or ECS 030 or ECS 036A).
courses.ge: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Computational Structural Bioinformatics
courses.description: Fundamental biological, chemical and algorithmic models underlying computational structural biology; protein structure and nucleic acids structure; comparison of protein structures; protein structure prediction; molecular simulations; databases and online services in computational structural biology.
courses.prerequisites: (BIS 002A or MCB 010); (ECS 010 or ECS 032A or or ECS 032AV or ECS 036A).

courses.title: Scientific Computation
courses.description: Matrix-vector approach using MATLAB for floating-point arithmetic, error analysis, data interpolation, least squares data fitting, quadrature, zeros, optimization and matrix eigenvalues and singular values. Parallel computing for matrix operations and essential matrix factorizations.
courses.prerequisites: (ECS 030 or ENG 006 or ECS 032A or ECS 032AV or ECS 010 or ECS 036A); (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067).

courses.title: Probability & Statistical Modeling for Computer Science
courses.description: Univariate and multivariate distributions. Estimation and model building. Markov/Hidden Markov models. Applications to data mining, networks, security, software engineering and bioinformatics.
courses.prerequisites: (ECS 040 or ECS 034 or ECS 036B);ECS 020;MAT 021C; (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067).

courses.title: Programming Languages
courses.description: Syntactic definition of programming languages. Introduction to programming language features including variables, data types, data abstraction, object-orientedness, scoping, parameter disciplines, exception handling. Non-imperative programming languages. Comparative study of several high-level programming languages.

courses.title: Programming Languages
courses.description: Continuation of programming language principles. Further study of programming language paradigms such as functional and logic; additional programming language paradigms such as concurrent (parallel); key implementation issues for those paradigms; and programming language semantics.

courses.title: Compilers
courses.description: Principles and techniques of lexical analysis, parsing, semantic analysis, code generation, and code optimization. Implementation of compilers.

courses.title: Scripting Languages & Their Applications
courses.description: Goals and philosophy of scripting languages, with Python and R as prime examples. Applications include networking, data analysis and display, and graphical user interfaces (GUIs).
courses.prerequisites: ECS 034 or ECS 036C or ECS 060; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Operating Systems & System Programming
courses.description: Basic concepts of operating systems and system programming. Processes and interprocess communication/synchronization; virtual memory, program loading and linking; file and I/O subsystems; utility programs. Study of a real operating system.
courses.prerequisites: (ECS 034 or ECS 036C or ECS 060); (ECS 154A or EEC 170).

courses.title: Computer Networks
courses.description: Overview of computer networks, TCP/IP protocol suite, computer-networking applications and protocols, transport-layer protocols, network architectures, Internet Protocol (IP), routing, link-layer protocols, local area and wireless networks, medium access control, physical aspects of data transmission, and network-performance analysis.
courses.prerequisites: (ECS 032B or ECS 036C); (ECS 132 or EEC 161 or MAT 135A or STA 032 or STA 035B or STA 100 or STA 131A).
courses.creditLimitations: Only 2 units of credit for students who have taken ECS 157.

courses.title: Computer Networks
courses.description: TCP/IP protocol suite, computer networking applications, client-server and peer-to-peer architectures, application-layer protocols, transport-layer protocols, transport-layer interfaces, sockets, network programming, remote procedure calls, and network management.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Computer Networks
courses.description: Advanced topics in computer networks, wireless networks, multimedia networking, traffic analysis and modeling, network design and management, network simulation and performance analysis, and design projects in communication networks.

courses.title: Computer Security
courses.description: Principles, mechanisms, and implementation of computer security and data protection. Policy, encryption and authentication, access control, and integrity models and mechanisms; network security; secure systems; programming and vulnerabilities analysis. Study of an existing operating system.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECS 155.

courses.title: Computer Architecture
courses.description: Introduction to digital design. Interfacing of devices for I/O, memory and memory management. Input/output programming, via wait loops, hardware interrupts and calls to operating system services. Hardware support for operating systems software.
courses.creditLimitations: Only 1 unit of credit allowed for students who have taken EEC 170.

courses.title: Computer Architecture
courses.description: Hardwired and microprogrammed CPU design. Memory hierarchies. Uniprocessor performance analysis under varying program mixes. Introduction to pipelining and multiprocessors.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have taken ECS 201A.

courses.title: Programming on Parallel Architectures
courses.description: Techniques for software development using the shared-memory and message-passing paradigms, on parallel architectures and networks of workstations. Locks, barriers, and other techniques for synchronization. Introduction to parallel algorithms.

courses.title: Software Engineering
courses.description: Requirements, specification, design, implementation, testing, and verification of large software systems. Study and use of software engineering methodologies.

courses.title: Modern Programming Tools
courses.description: Concepts and practice of collaborative software development using modern software tools.

courses.title: Web Programming
courses.description: Technical aspects of building websites, including both server-side and client-side software development.
courses.prerequisites: ECS 030 or ECS 034 or ECS 036B; or equivalent programming experience in C and the Unix environment.

courses.title: Information Visualization
courses.description: Exploration and communication of a variety forms of data through visualization. Design principles of human-computer interaction and data visualization techniques. Authentic practices in designing and evaluating interactive visualization systems to combat information overload and engage users in analytic thinking.

courses.title: Human-Computer Interaction
courses.description: Introduction to concepts and practice of modern human-computer interaction design.

courses.title: Database Systems
courses.description: Database modeling and design (E/R model, relational model), relational algebra, query languages (SQL), file and index structures, query processing, transaction management.

courses.title: Database Systems
courses.description: Data modeling (object-relational, graph-based, spatiotemporal models). Querying semistructured data (XML). Database theory (normalization, integration, provenance). Database programming (stored procedures, embedded SQL, web programming). Advanced topics (data warehousing, parallel data processing).

courses.title: Evaluating User Interactions
courses.description: Introduction to principles, processes, and methods for evaluating how users use and interact with computing systems and technologies.

courses.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Design and implementation of intelligent computer systems. Knowledge representation and organization. Memory and inference. Problem solving. Natural language processing.

courses.title: Machine Learning
courses.description: Introduction to machine learning. Supervised & unsupervised learning, including classification, dimensionality reduction, regression & clustering using modern machine learning methods. Applications of machine learning to other fields.
courses.prerequisites: (ECS 032B or ECS 036C); (STA 032 or STA 035B or STA 100 or STA 131A or MAT 135A or EEC 161 or ECS 132); (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067).

courses.title: Recommender Systems
courses.description: Collaborative filtering and content-based methods for building recommender systems. Statistical, matrix factorization, textual analysis, and nearest-neighbor approaches. Case studies.
courses.prerequisites: (ECS 032B or ECS 036B or ECS 040); (ECS 132 or STA 130A or STA 131A or ECN 140); (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067).

courses.title: Image Processing & Analysis
courses.description: Techniques for automated extraction of high-level information from images generated by cameras, three-dimensional surface sensors, and medical devices. Typical applications include detection of objects in various types of images and describing populations of biological specimens appearing in medical imagery.
courses.prerequisites: (MAT 067 C- or better or MAT 027A C- or better or MAT 022A C- or better); (ECS 060 or ECS 032B or ECS 036C).

courses.title: Computer Vision
courses.description: Computer vision is the study of enabling machines to "see" the visual world; e.g., understand images and videos. Explores several fundamental topics in the area, including feature detection, grouping and segmentation, and recognition.
courses.prerequisites: (ECS 060 or ECS 032B or ECS 036C); recommended (STA 032 or STA 131A or MAT 135A or EEC 161 or ECS 132); (MAT 022A or MAT 27A or MAT 067).

courses.title: Computer Graphics
courses.description: Principles of computer graphics, with a focus on interactive systems. Current graphics hardware, elementary operations in two-and three-dimensional space, geometric transformations, camera models and interaction, graphics system design, standard graphics APIs, individual projects.
courses.prerequisites: (ECS 060 or ECS 034 or ECS 036C); (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067).

courses.title: Scientific Visualization
courses.description: Computer graphics techniques for generating images of various types of measured or computer-simulated data. Typical applications for these graphics techniques include study of air flows around car bodies, medical data, and molecular structures.

courses.title: Geometric Modeling
courses.description: Interactive graphics techniques for defining and manipulating geometrical shapes used in computer animation, car body design, aircraft design, and architectural design.

courses.title: Gameplay Programming
courses.description: Developing gameplay systems in the context of game design and software engineering. Aspects of technical game development that depend on the genre or details of a specific game design, thus making them difficult to abstract and engineer into game engines.
courses.prerequisites: ECS 032B or ECS 036C; extensive programming experience recommended.

courses.title: Ethics in an Age of Technology
courses.description: Foundations of ethics. Views of technology. Technology and human values. Costs and benefits of technology. Character of technological change. Social context of work in computer science and engineering.
courses.ge: Social Sciences (SS); Scientific Literacy (SL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.description: Responding to real-life client design challenges, student teams plan, implement, and evaluate large-scale projects involving computer and computational systems. Project supervised by a faculty member. Must take ECS 193A&ECS 193B to receive credit.
courses.prerequisites: ECS 160(can be concurrent);ECS 150; upper division standing in Computer Science or Computer Science & Engineering; or consent of instructor.

courses.description: Responding to real-life client design challenges, student teams plan, implement, and evaluate large-scale projects involving computer and computational systems. Project supervised by a faculty member. Must take ECS 193A&ECS 193B to receive credit.

courses.description: Tutoring in computer science courses, especially introductory courses.

courses.description: Directed group study.

courses.description: Student facilitated course intended primarily for upper division students.

courses.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates.

courses.title: Student Facilitated Course Development
courses.description: Under the supervision of a faculty member, an undergraduate student plans and develops the course they will offer under 098F/198F.

courses.title: Student Facilitated Teaching
courses.description: STU FAC. Under the supervision of a faculty member, an undergraduate student teaches a course under 098F/198F.

courses.title: Advanced Computer Architecture
courses.description: Modern research topics and methods in computer architecture. Design implications of memory latency and bandwidth limitations. Performance enhancement via within-processor and between-processor parallelism.
courses.creditLimitations: One unit of credit if student has previously taken ECS 154B after Fall 2019.

courses.title: High-Performance Uniprocessing
courses.description: Maximizing uniprocessor performance. Barriers to high performance; solutions to the problems; historical and current processor designs.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECS 250B.

courses.title: Parallel Architectures
courses.description: Evolution of parallel architectures from special-purpose machines to commodity servers. Emphasis on recent machines and applications that drive them.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECS 250C.

courses.title: Novel Computing Technologies
courses.description: Novel computing technologies that could revolutionize computer architecture. Quantum computing technologies, including algorithms, devices, and fault tolerance. A survey of other unconventional technologies including nanoscale electronics, MEMS devices, biological devices, and nanotechnology.

courses.title: Theory of Computation
courses.description: Time and space complexity classes. Reductions, completeness, and the role of randomness. Logic and undecidability.

courses.title: Computational Methods in Systems & Synthetic Biology
courses.description: Computational methods related to systems and synthetic biology. An overview of machine learning techniques related to the analysis of biological data, biological networks. Predictive modeling and simulation of biological systems. Topics on biological circuit construction.

courses.title: Design & Analysis of Algorithms
courses.description: Techniques for designing efficient algorithms, analyzing their complexity and applying these algorithms to a broad range of applications. Methods for recognizing and dealing with difficult problems.

courses.title: Advanced Design & Analysis of Algorithms
courses.description: Advanced topics in complexity theory. Problem classification. The classes P, NP, P-space, co-NP. Matching and network flow algorithms. Matrix multiplication. Approximation algorithms.

courses.title: Parallel Algorithms
courses.description: Models of parallel computer systems including PRAMs, loosely coupled systems and interconnection networks. Parallel algorithms for classical problems and general techniques for their design and analysis. Proving lower bounds on parallel computation in several settings.

courses.title: String Algorithms & Applications in Computational Biology
courses.description: Algorithms that operate on strings. Pattern matching, sets of patterns, regular expression pattern matching, suffix trees and applications, inexact similarity, parametric sequence alignment, applications to DNA sequencing and protein database searching.

courses.title: Graph Theory
courses.description: Fundamental concepts. Planar graphs: Kuratowski's theorem. Packings and coverings. Menger's theorem, representation of cuts, Hamilton graphs, rigid graphs, chordal graphs, graph coloring, graph isomorphism, applications and some algorithms.
courses.prerequisites: graduate standing in electrical engineering or computer science or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Computational Geometry
courses.description: Mathematics of unstructured data. Algorithms for data structures such as Voronoi diagrams, oct-trees, and arrangements. Applications in computer graphics, concentrating on problems in three-dimensions.

courses.title: Modern Cryptography
courses.description: Modern cryptography as a discipline emphasizing formal definitions and proofs of security. One-way functions, pseudo-randomness, encryption, digital signatures, zero-knowledge, secure protocols.

courses.title: Cryptograpy for E-Commerce
courses.description: Cryptographic primitives and protocols of importance to e-commerce, present and future, including content distribution mechanisms, payment mechanisms, pricing mechanisms, anonymity and privacy mechanisms, fair exchange mechanisms.

courses.title: Advanced Computational Structural Bioinformatics
courses.description: Algorithmic problems in structural biology; protein structure classification; protein structure prediction (including comparative modeling and ab initio protein structure prediction); molecular simulations (molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations).

courses.title: Applied Numerical Linear Algebra
courses.description: Numerical linear algebra (NLA) with emphasis on applications in engineered systems; matrix factorizations; perturbation and rounding error analyses of fundamental NLA algorithms.

courses.title: Large-Scale Scientific Computation
courses.description: Algorithms and techniques for large-scale scientific computation, including basics for high performance computing, iterative methods, discrete approximation, fast Fourier transform, Poisson solvers, particle methods, spectral graph partition and its applications.

courses.title: Theory of Molecular Computation
courses.description: Theory of chemical reaction networks, molecular circuits, DNA self-assembly, DNA sequence design and thermodynamic energy models, and connections to the field of distributed computing.
courses.prerequisites: ECS 120 or ECS 220 recommended; probability course recommended, for example ECS 132 or MAT 135A or STA 012 or STA 131A or MAT 131A; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Computational Functional Genomics
courses.description: Bioinformatics methods for analysis and inference of functional relationships among genes using large-scale genomic data, including methods for integration of gene expression, promoter sequence, TF-DNA binding and other data, and approaches in modeling of biological networks.
courses.prerequisites: ECS 124; graduate standing in Computer Science or Life Sciences.

courses.title: Computer & Information Security
courses.description: Modern topics in computer security, including: protection, access control, operating systems security, network security, applied cryptography, cryptographic protocols, secure programming practices, safe languages, mobile code, malware, privacy and anonymity, and case studies from real-world systems.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have taken ECS 235.

courses.title: Foundations of Computer & Information Security
courses.description: Theoretical foundations of methods used to protect data in computer and communication systems. Access control matrix and undecidability of security; policies; Bell-LaPadula, Biba, Chinese Wall models; non-interference and non-deducibility; information flow and the confinement problem.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have taken ECS 235.

courses.title: Computer Security: Intrusion Detection Based Approach
courses.description: Concepts of intrusion detection, anomaly detection based on machine learning, signature-based detection using pattern matching, automated response to attacks using artificial intelligence planning, tracing intruders based on principal component analysis, security policy languages.

courses.title: Programming Languages
courses.description: Advanced topics in programming languages, including formal syntax and semantics, the relation between formal semantics and verification, an introduction to the lambda calculus. Additional topics will include language design principles, alternative programming languages, in-depth semantic theory and models of language implementation.

courses.title: Translation of Programming Languages
courses.description: Lexical analysis, parsing, storage management, symbol table design, semantic analysis and code generation. LR, LALR grammars. Compilercompilers.

courses.title: Code Generation & Optimization
courses.description: Compiler optimizations for performance, code size and power reduction. Topics include control- and data-flow analysis, redundancy elimination, loop and cache optimizations, register allocation, local and global instruction scheduling, and modulo scheduling.

courses.title: Principles of Concurrent Programming
courses.description: Fundamental concepts and applications of concurrent programs; concurrent program verification and derivation; synchronization mechanisms in programming languages; distributed programming techniques; case studies of languages.

courses.title: Analysis of Software Artifacts
courses.description: Techniques for the analysis of software artifacts, including source code, build processes, test suites, bug reports and documentation with a special emphasis on software correctness and performance in real-world settings.

courses.title: Concurrent Programming Languages
courses.description: Language design parameters. Models of parallel machines. Load balancing. Scalability. Portability. Efficiency measures. Design and implementation techniques for several classes of concurrent programming languages (such as object-oriented, functional, logic, and constraint programming languages).

courses.title: Operating Systems
courses.description: Models, design, implementation, performance evaluation in operating systems. Algorithms, internal architectures for single processor OS and distributed systems. Concurrency control, recovery, security. OS kernel-level programming. Special topics embedded systems, real-time system, device driver, NPU (Network Processor Unit).

courses.title: Computer Networks
courses.description: Internet protocol based computer networks applications, transport, network layer protocols. High speed LAN technologies: Ethernet, Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM). Delay models in data networks: analysis of multiaccess techniques in polling, ring, random access networks. Multimedia applications requirements and design.

courses.title: Network Theory & Applications
courses.description: Develops the mathematical theory underlying growth, structure and function of networks with applications to physical, social, biological and engineered systems. Topics include network growth, resilience, epidemiology, phase transitions, software and algorithms, routing and search control, cascading failures.
courses.prerequisites: MAT 022A;MAT 022B; (STA 013 or STA 013Y or STA 120); experience with computer software, or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Resource Management in Wireless Communication Networks
courses.description: Advanced research issues in wireless communication networks, including multi-user diversity and cross-layer optimization, basic network information theory, MIMO systems and the impact on networks, and dynamics spectrum management.

courses.title: Probability Models for Computer Science
courses.description: Probabilistic and statistical models useful in computer/data science. Applications to networks, bioinformatics, database management, machine learning, software engineering and image processing.
courses.prerequisites: A calculus-based course in probability, such as ECS132,STA 131A, or EEC 161; programming skills and familiarity with matrix algebra.
courses.activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Project, Extensive Problem Solving.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECS 256A.

courses.title: Mobile & Wireless Networks
courses.description: Fundamental techniques in design of second generation wireless networks: cellular network and protocols, medium access techniques, handoff control, signaling and mobility management, wireless data works, Internet mobility and Personal Communication Services (PCS). Third generation wideband systems, novel technologies, adhoc networks.

courses.title: Optical Networks
courses.description: Optical networks. Enabling technologies. Multiplexing techniques. WDM. Broadcast networks. Wavelength-routed networks. Network architectures. Protocols. Network algorithms. Device-network interface. Optimization problems.

courses.title: Software Engineering
courses.description: Advanced techniques for domain-specific software reuse.

courses.title: Program Verification
courses.description: Methods of proving correctness of programs with respect to formal specifications, with attention to those suited for employing automated deduction.Logic background, symbolic execution, techniques suited to iterative programming, methods from denotational semantics, termination, dynamic logic and proofs of concurrent programs.
courses.prerequisites: PHI 112; or MAT 125 or familiarity with first-order logic; knowledge of an integrative and functional programming language.

courses.title: Formal Specification
courses.description: Formal specification of modules, and its relationship to topdown programming development and verification. Abstract data types, together with methods for specifying them. Implementations and proofs of implementation. Using specifications to reason about programs. Parameterized types. Constructing good formal specifications.

courses.title: Distributed Database Systems
courses.description: Concepts of distributed database systems and architectures, distributed database design, distributed query processing and optimization, transaction management and concurrency control, heterogeneous and multidatabase systems.

courses.title: Spatial Databases
courses.description: Concepts, models, and architectures for spatial databases, spatial access methods, query processing, spatio-temporal data management, moving objects, spatial data mining.

courses.title: Wide-Area Distributed Information Systems
courses.description: Wide-area distributed information systems, data broadcast, multicast, publish/subscribe, service differentiation, information retrieval, Web caching.

courses.title: Scientific Data & Workflow Management
courses.description: Scientific data integration, metadata, knowledge representation, ontologies, scientific workflow design and management.

courses.title: Visual Recognition
courses.description: Graduate seminar course on computer vision with an emphasis on object recognition, activity recognition, and scene understanding.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Concepts and techniques underlying the design and implementation of models of human performance on intelligent tasks. Representation of high-level knowledge structures. Models of memory and inference. Natural language and story understanding. Common sense planning and problem solving.

courses.title: Machine Learning & Discovery
courses.description: Artificial intelligence techniques for knowledge acquisition by computers. Fundamental problems in machine learning and discovery. Systems that learn from examples, analogies, and solved problems. Systems that discover numerical laws and qualitative relationships. Projects centering on implementation and evaluation.

courses.title: Information Visualization
courses.description: Advanced topics in information visualization: perceptually effective display methods, color design and selection, interaction models and techniques, focus-context techniques, distortion methods, large graph visualization techniques, visual data mining methods, and evaluation methods.

courses.title: Visual Analytics
courses.description: Analytical reasoning using visual means, data and visual transformations, exploratory visualization, explanatory visualization, interactive intelligent systems, qualitative and quantitative evaluation.

courses.title: Automated Deduction
courses.description: Techniques of mechanical theorem proving. Methods based on resolution and termrewriting. Decision procedures. Induction. Applications to program verification, question/answering and plan generation. Study existing mechanical theorem provers.
courses.prerequisites: PHI 112; or MAT 125 or familiarity with first order logic.

courses.title: Advanced Computer Graphics
courses.description: Advanced topics in computer graphics. Hidden surface models, rendering of various surface types, subdivision methods, shading techniques, anti-aliasing, modeling techniques.

courses.title: Advanced Computer Graphics
courses.description: Advanced topics in computer graphics and geometric modeling. Topics taken from advanced research papers in computer graphics, image synthesis, visualization and geometric modeling. Discussion of current research in the field.

courses.title: Advanced Volume Visualization
courses.description: Applications, available tools and techniques, the challenges confronting the field of volume visualization, and some of the advanced topics in the field. Primary emphasis on advanced software and hardware techniques to achieve interactive visualization.

courses.title: Advanced Visualization
courses.description: Visualization of 3D data, including scalar fields, vector fields, and medical data.

courses.title: Computer-Aided Geometric Design
courses.description: Mathematical techniques for the definition and manipulation of curves and surfaces. Bezier curves and surfaces, B-spline curves and surfaces, subdivision surfaces, wavelets. Integration into various computer graphics rendering models, visualization systems and computer-aided design systems.

courses.title: Computer Animation
courses.description: Surveys current research and fundamental techniques that lie behind character animation tools. Emphasis on improving expressive aspects of movement and how physics, motion capture data, the arts and psychology literature, and interactive techniques can be used towards this goal.

courses.title: Virtual Reality Technology
courses.description: Fundamentals and principles of Virtual Reality (VR) technology. Potential and limits for its useful application. Developing a complete virtual reality application.

courses.title: Applied Research Methods for Human-Computer Interaction
courses.description: Quantitative methods for studying how people interact with computing and information systems, developing and evaluating systems that are driven by users' needs, constraints and goals involved in human-technology interactions.
courses.prerequisites: Courses or experience related to product development in mobile apps, websites, information systems, and/or AI tools recommended.

courses.title: Advanced Natural Language Processing
courses.description: Use of deep learning techniques in advanced natural language processing. Practicing advanced learning and inference techniques with large language models.
courses.prerequisites: ECS 171 or ECS 271; or equivalent machine learning course.

courses.title: Graduate Research Group Conference

courses.title: Research in Computer Science
courses.description: Study of research topics in computer science, Ph.D. level research methodologies (experimental, applied and theoretical). Study skills necessary to successfully find/solve significant research problems. Finding and successful interacting with a research advisor. Ethical issues in research/collaborative work.

courses.title: Research in Computer Science
courses.description: Study of Ph.D. level research methodologies (experimental, applied and theoretical), presenting research results for the computer science community. Study skills necessary to successfully find/solve significant research problems.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in computer science;ECS 293A recommended.

courses.description: Group study.

courses.title: The Teaching of Computer Science
courses.description: Participation as a teaching assistant or associate-in in a designated engineering course. Methods of leading discussion groups or laboratory sections, writing and grading quizzes, use of laboratory equipment, and grading laboratory reports.
courses.prerequisites: Meet qualifications for teaching assistant and/or associate-in in Computer Science.

courses.title: Teaching Assistant Training Practicum
courses.description: Teaching assistant training practicum.

courses.title: Introduction to Linguistics
courses.description: Introduction to the study of language; its nature, diversity, and structure.

courses.title: Introduction to Linguistics
courses.description: Introduction to the study of language; its nature, diversity, and structure.
courses.activities: Web Virtual Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
courses.creditLimitations: Students may not take both LIN 001 and LIN 001Y for credit.

courses.title: Language, the Mind, & Computers
courses.description: Analysis of human language and language processing by humans and machines. How language is represented and processed in the human mind, how computers process language, and similarities and differences between human and computer processing of language. Human-media interaction for language and society.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); Domestic Diversity (DD); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.description: Analysis of human language and language processing by humans and machines. How language is represented and processed in the human mind, how computers process language, and similarities and differences between human and computer processing of language. Human-media interaction for language and society.
courses.activities: Web Virtual Lecture 3 hour(s), Web Electronic Discussion 1 hour(s).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); Domestic Diversity (DD); Scientific Literacy (SL).
