courses.description: Analysis of human language and language processing by humans and machines. How language is represented and processed in the human mind, how computers process language, and similarities and differences between human and computer processing of language. Human-media interaction for language and society.
courses.activities: Web Virtual Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); Domestic Diversity (DD); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Language & the Body
courses.description: Perspectives on the role of language in issues about bodies. Language-related disabilities. Social implications of language use in discussing body-related conditions.

courses.title: Global English & Communication
courses.description: English as a global language and its uses in intercultural communication. Cultural, historical, and political dimensions of varieties of English spoken around the world. Experiential grounding in strategies for increasing interpretive and verbal communicative competence for a globalized world.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); Oral Skills (OL); World Cultures (WC).

courses.title: Language & Society
courses.description: Language as a social phenomenon. Topics include linguistic diversity, language policy, language and identity, language and social structure, speech communities and social networks, the effect of social factors on language variation, linguistic consequences of language contact.
courses.ge: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH); Domestic Diversity (DD); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Academic Oral Communication
courses.description: Structure of oral communication, critical thinking, and persuasion in classroom discourse in American English and in cross-cultural perspective.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); Oral Skills (OL).

courses.title: Directed Group Study in English as a Second Language
courses.description: Directed group study of topic in English as a Second Language (ESL).

courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Intended for lower division students.

courses.title: Special Study for Undergraduates
courses.description: Intended for lower division students.

courses.title: Linguistic Analysis I: Phonetics, Phonology, Morphology
courses.description: Introduction to fundamental methods and concepts used in linguistic analysis, focusing on phonetic, phonological, and morphological phenomena. Emphasizes development of analytical skills and appreciation of structural regularities and differences among languages.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed LIN 139.

courses.title: Linguistic Analysis II: Morphology, Syntax, Semantics
courses.description: Introduction to fundamental methods and concepts used in linguistic analysis, focusing on morphological, syntactic, and semantic phenomena. Emphasizes development of analytical skills and appreciation of structural regularities and differences among languages.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed LIN 140.

courses.title: Topics in Language & Linguistics
courses.description: Detailed examination of a major contemporary linguistic theory, a major contemporary issue or related set of issues in linguistics, or the structure of a particular language or language family.

courses.title: English Grammar
courses.description: Survey of present-day English grammar as informed by contemporary linguistic theories. The major syntactic structures of English; their variation across dialects, styles, and registers; their development; and their usefulness in describing the conventions of English.
courses.prerequisites: LIN 001 or LIN 001Y or ENG 003 or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Introduction to Phonological Theory
courses.description: Modern approaches to phonological theory with emphasis on considering a broad range of theoretical perspective in accounting for variation across and within languages.
courses.prerequisites: LIN 001 or LIN 001Y or LIN 103A recommended.

courses.title: Phonetics
courses.description: Detailed examination of articulatory and acoustic phonetics.

courses.title: Morphology
courses.description: Introduction to the analysis of word structure and the relation of word structure to the lexicon and other grammatical components.

courses.title: Text Processing & Corpus Linguistics
courses.description: Investigation of the lexical organization of human languages through corpus linguistics. Application of principles of linguistic analysis, automatic text processing, and statistical research to solving problems of textual evaluation and classification, as well as information retrieval and extraction.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); Quantitative Literacy (QL).

courses.title: Introduction to Syntactic Theory
courses.description: Introduction to syntactic theory, primarily through the examination of a major theory of syntax, emphasizing theoretical reasoning, argumentation, and problems of theory building in syntax.

courses.title: Semantics
courses.description: Linguistic study of meanings of words and phrases, meanings expressed by lexical items and compositional structures. Truth-conditional models of semantics, evaluated in context and against social conventions.

courses.title: Languages of the World
courses.description: Survey of the world's languages, their geographical distribution and classification, both genetic and typological. Illustrative descriptions of several major languages from different geographical areas; pidgins and creoles, lingua francas and other languages of widespread use.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed LIN 050.
courses.ge: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC).

courses.title: Historical Linguistics
courses.description: Description and methods of the historical study of language, including the comparative method and internal reconstruction; sound change, morphological change, syntactic change, semantic change.

courses.title: Language Universals & Typology
courses.description: Investigation into common features of all human languages and the classification of languages in terms of their structural features. Theories of universal grammar. Detailed discussion of non-Indo-European languages and comparison with English.

courses.title: American Voices
courses.description: Explores the forms of American English: traditional notions of regional dialects and increasingly important social dialects, reflecting age, class, gender, race, ethnicity, and sexual orientation. Influence of language attitudes on perception of dialect speakers; dialect in media, education, and literature.
courses.prerequisites: LIN 001 or LIN 001Y or ANT 004; or upper division standing recommended.

courses.title: Global Sociolinguistics
courses.description: Overview of key sociolinguistic concepts from a global perspective, focusing on language variation, language use and language policy. Processes of language maintenance, shift and change; the construction of identities in interactions through the use of dialects, styles, and registers. Cross-cultural communication and politeness.

courses.title: Language, Gender, & Society
courses.description: Investigation of real and putative (stereotyped) gender-linked differences in language structure and usage, with a consideration of some social and psychological consequences of such differences. Focus is on English, but other languages are also discussed.
courses.ge: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH); Domestic Diversity (DD); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Discourse Analysis
courses.description: Methods of analyzing spoken and written chunks of language as they happen in various contexts, including doctor's offices, classrooms, sports arenas, news media, etc.

courses.title: Introduction to Applied Linguistics
courses.description: Applications of linguistic principles and the analysis of language-related issues in the world. Exploration of a range of language-related problems including issues related to language learning and teaching to issues concerning language and gender, race, class and the media.

courses.title: The Spanish Language in the United States
courses.description: Linguistic features of the varieties of the Spanish language spoken throughout the United States; phonology, morphology, syntax, vocabulary. Focus on the relationship between United States Spanish and other world varieties of Spanish, within a historical framework.
courses.prerequisites: LIN 001 or LIN 001Y or SPA 111N;SPA 023; or equivalent to SPA 023 recommended.

courses.title: Introduction to Psycholinguistics
courses.description: Introduction to psychological issues relating to the implementation of language and linguistic structure during speech production and comprehension and to the implications of research in psychology and related fields for linguistic theory.

courses.title: Language Development
courses.description: Theory and research on children's acquisition of their native language, including the sound system, grammatical systems, and basic semantic categories.
courses.prerequisites: (LIN 001 or LIN 001Y); or consent of instructor;LIN 103A,103Brecommended.

courses.title: Biological Basis of Language
courses.description: Overview of issues in the field of neurolinguistics and techniques used to explore representation of language in the human brain.

courses.title: Computational Linguistics
courses.description: Understanding the nature of language through computer modeling of linguistic abilities. Relationships between human cognition and computer representations of cognitive processing.
courses.prerequisites: Consent of instructor;LIN 001 or LIN 001Y recommended.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have taken LIN 007.

courses.title: Second Language Learning & Teaching
courses.description: Psycholinguistic and sociolinguistic theories of second language learning. Connections between theoretical perspectives and pedagogical practices in formal and informal second language settings, with focus on tutoring. Impact of sociocontextual factors (e.g., gender, ethnicity). Fieldwork requirement.
courses.prerequisites: LIN 001 or LIN 001Y; or equivalent recommended.

courses.title: Multilingualism
courses.description: Issues in multilingualism from a global perspective: e.g., multilingual communities; multilingualism and identity (gender, ethnicity, nationality); language ideologies and educational and sociopolitical policies surrounding multilingualism; acquisition of multilingualism; discursive practices of multilinguals.
courses.ge: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Internship in Linguistics
courses.description: Internship applying linguistic-related skills to a fieldwork project in areas such as media, law, or industry, in approved organizations or institutions. Maximum of 4 units applicable toward major.
courses.prerequisites: LIN 001 or LIN 001Y; or equivalent course; consent of instructor.

courses.title: Special Study for Honors Students
courses.description: Guided research, under the direction of a faculty member approved by the Program Director, leading to a senior honors thesis.
courses.prerequisites: Consent of instructor; open only to linguistics majors of senior standing who qualify for Honors Program.

courses.title: Tutoring in Linguistics
courses.description: Leading of small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with one of the department's regular courses.
courses.prerequisites: Consent of instructor. Upper division standing and consent of department chairperson.

courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Directed group study.

courses.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates.

courses.title: Foundations of Linguistics I
courses.description: Survey of fundamental issues raised by pre-generative linguistics in the 20th century, with emphasis on issues crucial to applications of linguistics.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed LIN 203A.

courses.title: Foundations of Linguistics II
courses.description: Survey of fundamental issues raised by orthodox generative linguistics, with emphasis on issues crucial to applications of linguistics.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed LIN 203B.

courses.title: Foundations of Linguistics III
courses.description: Survey of fundamental issues raised by contemporary linguistic theories lying outside the generative grammar orthodoxy, with emphasis on issues crucial to applications of linguistics.

courses.title: Proseminar
courses.description: Introduction to research activity of faculty in the Graduate Group in Linguistics and guest speakers.

courses.title: Topics in Linguistic Theory & Methods
courses.description: Advanced study of current problems in linguistic theory and methodology.

courses.title: Topics in Linguistic Theory & Methods
courses.description: Advanced study of current problems in linguistic theory and methodology.

courses.description: Advanced study of current problems in linguistic theory and methodology.

courses.title: Topics in Linguistic Theory & Methods
courses.description: Advanced study of current problems in linguistic theory and methodology.

courses.title: Advanced Phonological Theory & Analysis
courses.description: Critical examination of current phonological theories.

courses.title: Advanced Phonetics
courses.description: Advanced investigation of the physiological basis of speech articulation and acoustic phonetics.

courses.title: Advanced Syntactic Theory & Analysis
courses.description: Critical survey of contemporary theories of syntax.

courses.title: Advanced Syntactic Theory & Analysis
courses.description: Advanced critical exploration of contemporary theories of linguistic semantics.

courses.title: Principles of Typological Linguistics
courses.description: Cross-linguistic comparison and typology, including word order, morphological typology, complex clauses, semantic categories and their grammaticalization, and applications of typology to language acquisition.

courses.title: Principles of Historical Linguistics
courses.description: Advanced analysis of the theory and methods of historical linguistics.

courses.title: Romance Linguistics
courses.description: Examination of the development of the Romance languages from Proto-Romance to the modern era. Application and critical examination of methods of historical and comparative linguistics in particular areas of structural change in Romance.

courses.title: Speech Perception
courses.description: Investigation into how listeners map a continuous and variable acoustic signal to a linguistic interpretation. Phonetic context, variation, linguistic knowledge, and sociolinguistics as factors in perceiving speech.

courses.title: Variation in Speech Communities
courses.description: Linguistic variability in time, space, and society. Theoretical issues related to social and linguistic constraints in variation; issues and methods in the quantitative analysis of variation. Speech community, quantitative analytic methods, and the scope of sociolinguistic competence.

courses.title: Discourse Analysis: Text in Context
courses.description: Introduction to and application of leading theoretical approaches to the analysis of discourse. Approaches to the analysis of (spoken and written) text in context, tools for analyzing different types of texts (narration, conversation, etc.). Theme/rheme, given/new, anaphora, discourse markers, and other lexical/grammatical features.

courses.title: Current Issues in Language & Gender
courses.description: Exploration of the construction and performance of gender through language in cross-cultural perspective and in a variety of contexts: informal conversations, narratives, workplaces, schools, households, the mass media. Special topics may include: language acquisition; multilingualism; ecofeminism; queer theory.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing; prior coursework in Linguistics, Gender Studies, or Cultural Studies is desirable; no expectation of bilingual proficiency.

courses.title: Language, Performance, & Power
courses.description: Exploration of the intersection between linguistic and social theories in the language-state relation and the performance of identity. Ideological sources of language differentiation; nation-building and linguistic difference. Political economic, sociolinguistic, and ethnographic approaches to understanding linguistic inequality.

courses.title: Computational Psycholinguistics
courses.description: Probabilistic models of psycholinguistic phenomena. Introduction to probability theory and Bayesian modeling. Linguistic phenomena covered include speech processing, sentence processing, pragmatics, and acquisition.

courses.title: Neurobiology of Language
courses.description: Survey of historical and modern conceptions of the neurobiology of language. Aphasia, functional neuroimaging, functional neuroanatomy of human language.

courses.title: Theories of Second Language Acquisition
courses.description: Covers theoretical perspectives that direct or have directed research in second language acquisition; explores the relationship between linguistics and language teaching and deals with the individual variables that influence second language learning.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Research Methods in TESOL/SLD
courses.description: Students will study a variety of research methods in second language research; evaluate research designs and methods of analyses, formulate research questions and hypotheses and design a study of their own, think about various kinds of data they can collect.

courses.title: Individual & Social Aspects of Bilingualism
courses.description: Broad overview of bi-and multilingualism, with focus on theoretical and descriptive research; topics covered range from language processing in bilinguals to code-switching to language as political issue in multilingual states.

courses.title: Politics of Bi & Multilingual Literacies
courses.description: Anthropological, psycho-social, political, and educational perspectives on bi- and multi-lingualism. Power, colonialism, "native/non-native" speakers, and varieties and the unequal distribution of social goods. Analysis of how competing factors keep peoples disenfranchised.

courses.title: Pedagogical Applications of Second Language Acquisition Theory
courses.description: Pedagogical implications of various theories of second language acquisition, facilitation of language acquisition in classroom settings, and techniques for conducting classroom-based research in language learning.

courses.title: English as a Second Language Teaching/Tutoring
courses.description: Teaching classes for ESL graduate students. Aiding the ESL undergraduate composition classes; tutoring foreign graduate student Teaching Assistants in pronunciation. Does not fulfill requirement toward the M.A. degree.
courses.prerequisites: LIN 300 or LIN 301 or LIN 302(can be concurrent); consent of instructor.

courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Directed group study.

courses.title: Research
courses.description: Research.

courses.title: Language Pedagogy
courses.description: Methods of teaching second languages to nonnative speakers, stressing particularly recent linguistic methodology and techniques, as related to teaching and tutoring in the UC Davis ESL program.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Linguistics or consent of instructor; concurrent enrollment in LIN 297T recommended.

courses.title: Teaching Academic Literacy
courses.description: Methods of teaching advanced academic literacy in a second language, with a focus on ESL composition. Lesson development, teaching and tutoring in the UC Davis ESL program.
courses.prerequisites: LIN 300; or consent of instructor; graduate standing.
courses.activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Tutorial 14 hour(s), Project, Practice.

courses.title: Recent Research & Special Projects in TESOL
courses.description: Review of recent research in second language acquisition and the teaching of English to speakers of other languages. Continued teaching and tutoring in the UC Davis ESL clinic. Each student designs and reports on a classroom research project.

courses.title: Second Language Literacy & Technology
courses.description: Exploration of literacy theory and critical pedagogy in relation to new instructional and communication technologies. Practicum experience in teaching second language literacy; reflection on connections between theory and practice. Fieldwork requirement.
courses.prerequisites: LIN 002 or equivalent coursework/experience in second language pedagogy; consent of instructor; graduate students only.
courses.activities: Lecture/Discussion 1.50 hour(s), Web Electronic Discussion 1.50 hour(s).

courses.title: Language Pedagogy for Teacher Educators
courses.description: Current issues in second language pedagogy, with a focus on communicative methodology, participatory curriculum design, academic literacy, and the social contexts of teaching. Emphasis on reflective teaching and action research. Mentoring of new language teachers.
courses.prerequisites: Admission to Ph.D. program in Linguistics or Foreign Languages, or permission of instructor; significant language teaching experience.

courses.title: Teaching Assistant Training Practicum
courses.description: Teaching assistant training.

courses.title: Elementary Algebra (no credit)
courses.description: Basic concepts of algebra, including polynomials, factoring, equations, graphs, and inequalities. Offered only if sufficient number of students enroll.

courses.title: Trigonometry (no credit)
courses.description: Basic concepts of trigonometry, including trigonometric functions, identities, inverse functions, and applications. Offered only if sufficient number of students enroll.

courses.title: Intermediate Algebra (no credit)
courses.description: Basic concepts of algebra, prepares student for college work in mathematics, such as MAT 016A or MAT 021A. Functions, equations, graphs, logarithms, and systems of equations. Offered only if sufficient number of students enroll.

courses.title: Precalculus
courses.description: Topics selected for their use in calculus, including functions and their graphs, slope, zeroes of polynomials, exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric functions, sketching surfaces and solids.
courses.prerequisites: Two years of high school algebra, plane geometry, plane trigonometry; obtaining required score on the Precalculus Diagnostic Examination.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed any of MAT 016A, MAT 016B, MAT 016C,MAT 017A,MAT 017B,MAT 017C,MAT 021A,MAT 021B, or MAT 021C with a C- or better.

courses.title: Calculus for Biology & Medicine
courses.description: Introduction to differential calculus via applications in biology and medicine. Limits, derivatives of polynomials, trigonometric, and exponential functions, graphing, applications of the derivative to biology and medicine.
courses.prerequisites: Two years of high school algebra, plane geometry, plane trigonometry, and analytical geometry, and satisfying the Mathematics Placement Requirement.

courses.prerequisites: PHY 080;PHY 104A;PHY 105A;PHY 110A;PHY 110B(can be concurrent);PHY 115A(can be concurrent); and consent of department.

courses.title: Formation of Galaxies & Cosmic Structures
courses.description: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Course Description:Formation of the cosmic web, including dark-matter halos and galaxies within them. Components of the Universe (dark matter, gas, stars) and their dynamical evolution. Gravitational collapse and virialization. Gas dynamics, heating, and cooling. Galactic star formation and stellar dynamics. Emphasis on theoretical concepts, computational methods, and simulations.
courses.prerequisites: (PHY 009A or PHY 009HAC- or better); (PHY 009B or PHY 009HBC- or better); (PHY 009C or PHY 009HCC- or better); (PHY 009D or PHY 009HDC- or better);PHY 104A C- or better;PHY 105A C- or better; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Environmental Physics & Society
courses.description: Impact of humankind on the environment are discussed from the point of view of the physical sciences. Calculations based on physical principles will be made, and the resulting policy implications are considered.
courses.prerequisites: (PHY 009D or PHY 007C); (PHY 010 or PHY 001B); MAT 016B; or the equivalent.

courses.title: Alumni Seminar Series
courses.description: Weekly guest speakers (usually a physics alumnus or alumna) tell students about their careers. Speakers use their experience to give students valuable perspectives on life after a degree in physics.

courses.title: Careers in Physics
courses.description: Overview of important research areas in physics, discussions of research opportunities and internships, strategies for graduate school and industrial careers, the fellowship and assistantship selection process, preparation of resumes, personal statements, and letters of recommendation.

courses.title: Internship in Physics
courses.description: Supervised work experience requiring the application of physics principles and techniques in a professional setting, including but not limited to industry and national laboratories.

courses.title: Senior Thesis
courses.description: Open only to Physics and Applied Physics majors with senior standing. Preparation of a senior thesis on a topic selected by the student with approval of the department.

courses.title: Tutoring in Physics & Astronomy
courses.description: Tutoring of students in lower division courses. Leading of small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with one of the department's regular courses. Weekly meeting with instructor.

courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Directed group study.

courses.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates.

courses.title: Theory of Mechanics & Electromagnetics
courses.description: Theoretical approaches in classical mechanics including the use of generalized coordinates and virtual work; variational calculus; Lagrange equations; symmetries, conservation laws, and Noether theorem; Lagrangian density; Hamilton formalism; canonical transformations; Poisson brackets; and Hamilton-Jacobi equations.
courses.prerequisites: PHY 204A(can be concurrent);PHY 104B;PHY 105B;PHY 110C; or equivalent to PHY 110C;PHY 204A required concurrently.

courses.title: Theory of Mechnics & Electromagnetics
courses.description: Theoretical approaches in electromagnetics including static electromagnetic fields; Maxwell's equations; plane waves in various media; magnetohydrodynamics; diffraction theory; radiating systems; and special relativity.

courses.title: Theory of Mechanics & Electromagnetics
courses.description: Theoretical approaches in electromagnetics including static electromagnetic fields; Maxwell's equations; plane waves in various media; magnetohydrodynamics; diffraction theory; radiating systems; and special relativity.

courses.title: Methods of Mathematical Physics
courses.description: Linear vector spaces, operators and their spectral analysis, complete sets of functions, complex variables, functional analysis, Greens functions, calculus of variations, introduction to numerical analysis.

courses.title: Methods of Mathematical Physics
courses.description: Linear vector spaces, operators and their spectral analysis, complete sets of functions, complex variables, functional analysis, Green's functions, calculus of variations, introduction to numerical analysis.

courses.title: Computational Physics
courses.description: Analytic techniques to solve differential equations and eignevalue problems. Physics content of course will be self-contained, and adjusted according to background of students.

courses.title: Quantum Mechanics
courses.description: Formal development and interpretation of non-relativistic quantum mechanics; its application to atomic, nuclear, molecular, and solid-state problems; brief introduction to relativistic quantum mechanics and the Dirac equation.

courses.title: Quantum Mechanics
courses.description: Formal development and interpretation of non-relativistic quantum mechanics; its application to atomic, nuclear, molecular, and solid-state problems; brief introduction to relativistic quantum mechanics and the Dirac equation.

courses.title: Quantum Mechanics
courses.description: Formal development and interpretation of non-relativistic quantum mechanics; its application to atomic, nuclear, molecular, and solid-state problems; brief introduction to relativistic quantum mechanics and the Dirac equation.

courses.title: Statistical Mechanics
courses.description: Foundations of thermodynamics and classical and quantum statistical mechanics with simple applications to properties of solids, real gases, nuclear matter, etc. and a brief introduction to phase transitions.
courses.activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Extensive Problem Solving 1 hour(s).

courses.title: Statistical Mechanics
courses.description: Further applications of thermodynamics and classical and quantum statistical mechanics. The modern theory of fluctuations about the equilibrium state, phase transitions and critical phenomena.
courses.activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Extensive Problem Solving 1 hour(s).

courses.title: Group Theoretical Methods of Physics-Condensed Matter
courses.description: Theory of groups and their representations with applications in condensed matter.
courses.prerequisites: PHY 215A;PHY 215B;PHY 215C(can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.PHY 215C required concurrently.

courses.title: Group Theoretical Methods of Physics-Elementary Particles
courses.description: Theory of groups and their representations with applications in elementary particle physics.
courses.prerequisites: PHY 215A;PHY 215B;PHY 215C(can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.PHY 215C required concurrently.

courses.title: Nuclear Physics
courses.description: Comprehensive study of the nucleon-nucleon interaction including the deuteron, nucleon-nucleon scattering, polarization, determination of real parameters of Smatrix, and related topics.

courses.title: Nuclear Physics
courses.description: Study of nuclear models, including shell model, collective model, unified model. Energy level spectra, static momenta, and electromagnetic transition rates.

courses.title: Nuclear Physics
courses.description: Study of nuclear scattering and reactions including the optical model and direct interactions. Beta decay and an introduction to weak interactions.

courses.title: Advanced Nuclear Theory
courses.description: Advanced topics in nuclear theory; theory of quantum-mechanical scattering processes. Exact formal theory and models for two-body scattering.

courses.title: Advanced Nuclear Theory
courses.description: Advanced topics in nuclear theory; theory of quantum-mechanical scattering processes. Exact formal theory and models for three-body scattering.

courses.title: Quantum Theory of Fields
courses.description: Relativistic quantum mechanics of particles; techniques and applications of second quantization; Feynman diagrams; renormalization.

courses.title: Quantum Theory of Fields
courses.description: Continuation of 230A, with selected advanced topics, such as S-matrix theory, dispersion relations, axiomatic formulations.

courses.title: Quantum Theory of Fields
courses.description: Renormalization theory and applications, including dimensional regularization, Ward identities, renormalization group equations, coupling constant unification, and precision electroweak calculations.

courses.title: Topics in String Theory
courses.description: Current research trends in string theory, with topics ranging from perturbative worldsheet methods, nonperturbative aspects and dualities, AdS/CFT correspondence, string field theory, etc.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor;PHY 230A,PHY 230B,PHY 230C&PHY 260 or equivalent are strongly recommended.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Geometry & Physics
courses.description: Modern geometric methods in theoretical physics, with topics ranging from from pseudo-Riemannian differential geometry and topology with application to general relativity, black holes, and string theory.

courses.title: Condensed Matter Physics A
courses.description: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Course Description:Topics in condensed matter physics: Crystal structure; one-electron theory; transport and optical properties of semiconductors; phonons, electron-phonon scattering.

courses.title: Condensed Matter Physics B
courses.description: Topics in condensed matter physics: transport and optical properties of metals and quantum structures; experimental measurement the Fermi surface and of phonon spectra.

courses.title: Condensed Matter Physics
courses.description: Review of second quantization. Interacting electron gas, electron-phonon interaction and effects, including instabilities of electronic systems. Topics in the theory of superconductivity and magnetism.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Magnetism
courses.description: Topics chosen from areas of current research interest.
courses.prerequisites: PHY 240A;PHY 240B;PHY 240C; PHY 240D; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Superconductivity
courses.description: Topics chosen from areas of current research interest.
courses.prerequisites: PHY 240A;PHY 240B;PHY 240C; PHY 240D; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Surface Physics of Materials
courses.description: Experimental and theoretical fundamentals of surface and interface physics and chemistry, including electronic and magnetic structure, thermodynamics, adsorption kinetics, epitaxial growth, and a discussion of various spectroscopic and structural probes based on photons, electrons, ions, and scanning probes.
courses.prerequisites: PHY 140A;PHY 140B;PHY 115A;PHY 115B; or the equivalent to any;PHY 215A,PHY 240A, or the equivalents recommended.

courses.title: Surface Physics of Materials
courses.description: Experimental and theoretical fundamentals of surface and interface physics and chemistry, including electronic and magnetic structure, thermodynamics, adsorption kinetics, epitaxial growth, and a discussion of various spectroscopic and structural probes based on photons, electrons, ions, and scanning probes.
courses.prerequisites: PHY 140A;PHY 140B;PHY 115A;PHY 115B; or the equivalent to any;PHY 215A,PHY 240A, or the equivalents recommended.

courses.title: Surface Physics of Materials
courses.description: Experimental and theoretical fundamentals of surface and interface physics and chemistry, including electronic and magnetic structure, thermodynamics, adsorption kinetics, epitaxial growth, and a discussion of various spectroscopic and structural probes based on photons, electrons, ions, and scanning probes.
courses.prerequisites: PHY 140A;PHY 140B;PHY 115A;PHY 115B; or the equivalent to any;PHY 215A,PHY 240A, or equivalents recommended.

courses.title: High-Energy Physics
courses.description: Phenomenology and systematics of strong, electromagnetic, and weak interactions of hadrons and leptons; determination of quantum numbers; quarks and quarkonia; deep inelastic scattering; the quark parton model; experiments at hadron colliders and electron-positron colliders.

courses.title: High-Energy Physics
courses.description: Electroweak interactions; phenomenology of the Standard Model of SU(2)LxU(1); weak interaction experiments; properties of and experiments with W and Z vector bosons; Glashow-Weinberg-Salam model and the Higgs boson; introduction to supersymmetry and other speculations.

courses.title: Collider Physics
courses.description: Collider physics. Topics include quark and gluon distribution functions and the computation of cross sections; Large Hadron Collider and International Linear Collider phenomenology; collider and detector characteristics; extracting models from data; software tools for analyzing experimental data.
courses.prerequisites: PHY 245A;PHY 252B(can be concurrent); or consent of instructor;PHY 252B taken previously or concurrently.

courses.title: Supersymmetry: Theory & Phenomenology
courses.description: Construction of supersymmetric models of particle physics; superfields; supersymmetry breaking the minimal supersymmetric standard model; supergravity. Collider phenomenology of supersymmetry. Dark matter phenomenology.
courses.prerequisites: PHY 230A,PHY 230B,PHY 245A,PHY 245B recommended, or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Supersymmetry: Theory & Phenomenology
courses.description: Construction of supersymmetric models of particle physics; superfields; supersymmetry breaking the minimal supersymmetric standard model; supergravity. Collider phenomenology of supersymmetry. Dark matter phenomenology. Not offered every year.
courses.prerequisites: PHY 230A;PHY 230B;PHY 245A,PHY 245B recommended or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Advanced Supersymmetry
courses.description: Advanced topics in supersymmetry. Topics include holomorphy, the Affleck-Dine-Seiberg superpotential, Seiberg duality for SUSY QCD, dynamical SUSY breaking, Seiberg-Witten theory, superconformal field theories, supergravity, anomaly and gaugino mediation, and the AdS/CFT correspondence.

courses.title: Special Topics in Physics
courses.description: Topic varies.

courses.title: Techniques of Experimental Physics
courses.description: Introduction to techniques and methods of designing and executing experiments. Problems and examples from condensed matter research will be utilized.

courses.title: Techniques of Experimental Physics
courses.description: Introduction to techniques and methods of designing and executing experiments. Problems and examples from nuclear and particle research will be utilized.

courses.title: Statistics & Data Analysis for Particle Physics
courses.description: Introduction to statistical data analysis methods in particle physics. Theoretical lectures combined with practical computer laboratory work.

courses.title: Signals & Noise in Physics
courses.description: Techniques for extracting signals from noise, systematic error.

courses.title: Econophysics
courses.description: Application of ideas from statistical mechanics to the financial markets. Market dynamics from a physics and systems perspective, including the statistical distributions of returns, the dynamics of prices, and models for the markets.
courses.prerequisites: Knowledge of Python, R, Excel, Matlab, or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Physics of Information
courses.description: Nonlinear dynamics, deterministic chaos, bifurcations, pattern formation, symbolic dynamics, measurement theory, stochastic processes, elementary information theory, information in complex systems, computational laboratory.
courses.prerequisites: Consent of instructor; advanced undergraduate or introductory graduate differential equations, applied linear algebra, and probability theory; e.g.,MAT 119A/MAT 119B or MAT 207A,MAT 167 or MAT 226A, and MAT 135A/MAT 135B or MAT 235A, respectively; or in PHY 104A/PHY 104B/PHY 104C or PHY 204A/PHY 204B.

courses.title: Physics of Computation
courses.description: Structural complexity, computational mechanics, information measures, causal inference, applications to complex materials, quantum dynamics, and nonequilibrium thermodynamics, computational laboratory.
courses.prerequisites: PHY 256A; consent of instructor; advanced undergraduate or introductory graduate differential equations, applied linear algebra, and probability theory; e.g.,MAT 119A/MAT 119B or MAT 207A,MAT 167 or MAT 226A, and MAT 135A/MAT 135B or MAT 235A, respectively; or in PHY 104A/PHY 104B/PHY 104C or PHY 204A/PHY 204B.

courses.title: Introduction to General Relativity
courses.description: An introduction to general relativity. Differential geometry and curved spacetime; the Einstein field equations; gravitational fields of stars and black holes; weak fields and gravitational radiation; experimental tests; Big Bang cosmology.

courses.title: Foundations of Astrophysics & Cosmology
courses.description: Foundational observations and models of astrophysics and cosmology. Photometry; spectroscopy; distance, velocity, and mass measurements; orbits, dark matter, and black holes; Friedmann-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker cosmology.
courses.prerequisites: PHY 105A B- or better;PHY 110A B- or better;PHY 115A B- or better.

courses.title: Early Universe Cosmology
courses.description: Introduction to early universe cosmology: the Big Bang, inflation, primordial nucleosynthesis, dark matter, dark energy, and other topics of current interest.
courses.prerequisites: Second year standing in Physics Graduate Program or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Cosmic Structure Formation
courses.description: Growth of structure from small density inhomogeneities in the early universe to the diverse structures observable today. Use of observable properties (cosmic microwave background, gravitational lensing, peculiar velocities, number density, etc.) to constrain models of structure formation and fundamental physics.

courses.title: High Energy Astrophysics & Radiative Processes
courses.description: Survey covering galactic and extragalactic X-ray and gamma-ray astronomy, radiative processes, and techniques of high-energy astrophysics.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Data Analysis for Astrophysics
courses.description: Survey covering measurement and signal analysis techniques for astrophysics and cosmology throughout the electromagnetic spectrum.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Observational Extragalactic Astronomy & Cosmology
courses.description: Survey covering current areas of research on extragalactic objects, their physical properties, origin, evolution, and distribution in space.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Research Methods in Astrophysics
courses.description: Introduction to research methods in astrophysics and cosmology. Problems and examples from observational and theoretical work will be included.

courses.title: Stellar Structure & Evolution
courses.description: Underlying physics of stars as the building blocks of the Universe. Reasons for their existence, mechanisms behind their function, their evolution and ultimate fate. Structure of self-gravitating objects, energy transport in stars, nuclear fusion in stars, stellar evolution, and the birth of compact objects.
courses.prerequisites: PHY 200A,PHY 200B, and PHY 215A recommended; graduate standing in Physics; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Current Topics in Physics Research
courses.description: Reading and discussion to help physics graduate students develop and maintain familiarity with the current and past literature in their immediate field of research and related areas.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Careers in Physics
courses.description: Designed to give Physics graduate students an in-depth appreciation of career opportunities with a graduate degree in physics. Professional physicists, mainly from outside academia, will give seminars describing both research and career insights.

courses.title: Seminar in Physics
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of topics of current research interest in physics. Topics will vary weekly and will cover a broad spectrum of the active fields of physics research at a level accessible to all physics graduate students.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

courses.description: Presentation and discussion of topics of current research interest in nuclear physics.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Seminar in Elementary Particle Physics
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of topics of current research interest in elementary particle physics.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

courses.title: High Energy Frontier Initiative & Cosmology Theory Seminar
courses.description: Weekly seminar on current issues in Particle physics and Cosmology.

courses.title: Seminar in Condensed Matter Physics
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of topics of current research interest in condensed matter physics.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Seminar in Cosmology
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of topics of current research interest in Cosmology.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Introduction to Departmental Research
courses.description: Seminar to introduce first- and second-year physics graduate students to the fields of specialty and research of the Physics staff.

courses.title: Field, Strings, & Gravity Seminar
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of topics of current research interest in the areas of quantum field theory, string theory and gravity.

courses.title: Research on the Teaching & Learning of Physics
courses.description: Discussion and analysis of recent research in how students construct understanding of physics and other science concepts and the implications of this research for instruction.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

courses.description: Analysis of recent research on science/physics teaching and learning and its implications for teaching labs, discussions, and discussion/labs with an emphasis on differences between conventional and active-engagement instructional settings. The appropriate role of the instructor in specific instructional settings.

courses.title: Methods of Teaching Physics
courses.description: Practical experience in methods and problems related to teaching physics laboratories at the university level, including discussion of teaching techniques, analysis of quizzes and laboratory reports and related topics. Required of all Physics Teaching Assistants.
courses.prerequisites: Consent of instructor; graduate standing in Physics.

courses.title: Teaching Assistant Training Practicum
courses.description: Teaching assistant training.

Transforming data, describing data, producing graphs, visual reasoning, and interpretations.
courses.activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Laboratory 1.50 hour(s), Web Virtual Lecture 1.50 hour(s).

courses.title: Freshman Psychology Seminar
courses.description: Instructor will acquaint students with his or her program of research, the development of scientific questions from the literature, and the application of research methods to examine these questions. Critical thinking will be encouraged via expository writing and brief presentations.

courses.title: Research Methods in Psychology
courses.description: Introduction to experimental design, interviews, questionnaires, field and observational methods, reliability, and statistical inference.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V);PSC 012Y or STA 013 or STA 100 strongly recommended.

courses.title: Mindreading: Understanding Other Minds
courses.description: Psychological perspectives on the process of understanding other peopleâs minds. Integration of social-cognitive theories with empirical evidence to explore the human ability to make sense of others' thoughts, feelings, and behaviors.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (SOC 001 or SOC 001V or PHI 010).

courses.title: Lower Division Seminar
courses.description: Examination of a special topic in Psychology through shared readings, discussions, written assignments, or special activities such as fieldwork or laboratory work.
courses.prerequisites: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

courses.description: Introduction to human information processing, mental representation and transformation, imagery, attention, memory, language processing, concept formation, problem solving, and computer simulation.
