courses.description: Survey and integration of the relationships between behavior and biological processes, including physiology, genes, development, ecology, and evolution. May be taught abroad.
courses.creditLimitations: Only 2 units of credit for those students who have completed NPB 100.

courses.title: Statistical Analysis of Psychological Data
courses.description: Design and statistical analysis of psychological investigations and the interpretation of quantitative data in psychology.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (STA 013 or STA 013Y or STA 032 or STA 100 or STA 102).
courses.activities: Lecture 4 hour(s), Laboratory 2 hour(s), Term Paper.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 103.

courses.title: Statistical Analysis of Psychological Data
courses.description: Probability theory, sampling distributions, statistical inference, and hypothesis testing using standard parametric and correlational approaches. Simple regression analysis, multiple regression analysis, non-parametric statistics, introduction to multivariate statistics, with applications in psychology.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 105.

courses.title: Applied Psychometrics: An Introduction to Measurement Theory
courses.description: Examination of the basic principles and applications of classical and modern test theory. Topics include test construction, reliability theory, validity theory, factor analysis and latent trait theory.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 041 or PSC 041V);PSC 103A; (STA 013 or STA 013Y); upper division standing in Psychology.

courses.title: Questionnaire & Survey Research Methods
courses.description: Introduction to survey and questionnaire research methods with emphasis on how to ask questions. Social and psychological factors that influence survey response. Practical aspects of fielding survey and questionnaire research.
courses.prerequisites: PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V; and consent of instructor;PSC 041 or an equivalent course on social or behavioral research methods or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Developmental Psychobiology
courses.description: The biology of behavioral development; survey and integration of the organismic and environmental processes that regulate the development of behavior.

courses.title: Agent-Based Modeling
courses.description: Introduction to agent-based computer simulation and analysis with emphasis on learning how to model animals, including humans, to achieve insight into social and group behavior.

courses.title: Physiological Psychology
courses.description: Relationship of brain structure and function to behavior, motivation, emotion, language, and learning in humans and other animals. An introduction to the methodology of physiological psychology and neuroscience.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed former PSC 108.

courses.title: Advanced Animal Behavior
courses.description: Advanced integrative survey of biological principles of behavioral organization, emphasizing historical roots, current research directions, conceptual issues and controversies. Laboratory exercises on the description and analysis of the behavior of captive and free-living animals
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed former PSC 150.

courses.title: Hormones & Behavior
courses.description: Endocrine physiology with an emphasis on the principles of behavior. Fundamental relationships between hormones and various behaviors engaged in by the organism during its lifetime. Role of hormones in behavioral homeostasis, social behavior, reproductive behavior, parental behavior, adaptation to stress.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed former PSC 152.

courses.title: Comparative Neuroanatomy
courses.description: Overview of the neuroanatomy in mammalian vertebrates, focusing on the cerebral cortex and experimental techniques. Examine changes or modifications to neural structures as a result of morphological or behavioral specializations.
courses.prerequisites: NPB 100 or NPB 101 or NPB 110B or PSC 121.

courses.title: Comparative Neuroanatomy Laboratory
courses.description: Comparative neuroanatomy laboratory illustrating modern neuroanatomical techniques in determining neural connections within the mammalian brain. Includes experimentation and presentation of results.

courses.title: Behavioral Epigenetics
courses.description: Review of basic principles in genetics and epigenetics with emphasis on behavior. Introduction to the use of modern molecular methods in understanding the complex relationships between genes, environment, and behavior.

courses.title: Health Psychology
courses.description: Psychological factors influencing health and illness. Topics include stress and coping, personality and health, symptom perception and reporting, heart disease, cancer, compliance, and health maintenance and promotion.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V);PSC 101 recommended.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed former PSC 160.

courses.title: Human Learning & Memory
courses.description: Consideration of major theories of human learning and memory with critical examination of relevant experimental data.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 012Y or STA 013 or STA 013Y or STA 100); or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Perception
courses.description: Cognitive organizations related to measurable physical energy changes mediated through sensory channels. Perception of objects, space, motion, events.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 100 or PSC 100Y or PSC 135).

courses.title: Language & Cognition
courses.description: Introduction to the cognitive processes involved in language comprehension and production. Topics include the biological foundations of language, speech perception, word recognition, syntax, reading ability, and pragmatics.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 100 or PSC 100Y or PSC 135); or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Neuroeconomics/Reinforcement Learning & Decision Making
courses.description: Theoretical and empirical approaches to neuroeconomics (neuroscience of decision making) from psychology, neuroscience, economics, and computer science. Neuroscience of judgment and decision making, behavioral economics, and reinforcement learning.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 100 or PSC 100Y or PSC 135 or ARE 100A or ECN 100A or ECN 100AV or NPB 162 or NPB 163); (STA 013 or STA 013Y or STA 100 or PSC 103A); or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Computational Cognitive Neuroscience
courses.description: Explorations of how brain secretes mind, via computer simulations that are manipulated and probed to investigate how neurons produce perception, attention, memory, language, and cognitive control.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V);PSC 100 or PSC 101 or PSC 135 recommended.

courses.title: Cognitive Neuroscience: The Biological Foundations of the Mind
courses.description: Neuroscientific foundations of higher mental processes including attention, memory, language, higher-level perceptual and motor processes, and consciousness. Emphasis on the neural mechanisms which form the substrates of human cognition and the relationship of mind to brain. May be taught abroad.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); or consent of instructor;PSC 101 or PSC 121 recommended.

courses.title: Psychology of Music
courses.description: Introduction to the mental and neural representations of musical structures and processes involved in perceiving, remembering, and performing music. Music and emotion.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 100 or PSC 100Y or PSC 135 or MUS 006C); or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Neurobiology of Learning & Memory
courses.description: Overview of the neural basis of learning and memory focusing on modern behavioral neuroscience research with animals. Topics include consolidation, neural plasticity, cellular competition for memory storage, and the role of neurogenesis in learning.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V);PSC 101.

courses.title: Consciousness & Cognition
courses.description: Current theoretical and empirical evidence in the study of cognition and consciousness. Theories of consciousness, psychological and neural basis of conscious and unconscious processes such as attention, intentionality, and dreams.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 100 or PSC 100Y or PSC 135).

courses.title: Advanced Cognitive Neuroscience
courses.description: Advanced integrative survey of cognitive neuroscience, including perception, attention, memory, and navigation. Emphasis on reviewing literature in psychology, neuroscience, and statistics; understanding methods in cognition; and presentation skills.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V);PSC 135; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Developmental Psychology
courses.description: An ontogenetic account of human behavior through adolescence with emphasis on motor skills, mental abilities, motivation, and social interaction.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).
courses.creditLimitations: Only 2 units of credit allowed to students who have completed HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B; not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 112. (Former PSC 112.)

courses.title: Developmental Psychology
courses.description: Ontogenetic account of human behavior through adolescence with emphasis on motor skills, mental abilities, motivation, and social interaction.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).
courses.activities: Web Virtual Lecture 3 hour(s(, Web Electronic Discussion 1 hour(s).
courses.creditLimitations: Only 2 units of credit allowed to students who have completed HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B; not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 112. (Former PSC 112.)

courses.title: Developmental Psychology
courses.description: Ontogenetic account of human behavior through adolescence with emphasis on motor skills, mental abilities, motivation, and social interaction.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).
courses.activities: Discussion 1 hour(s), Lecture 1.50 hour(s), Web Virtual Lecture.
courses.creditLimitations: Only 2 units of credit allowed to students who have completed HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B; not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 112. (Former PSC 112.)

courses.title: Cognitive Development
courses.description: Theories, methods, evidence, and debates in the field of cognitive development, such as nature/nurture, constraints on learning, and the role of plasticity. Topics include attention, memory, concepts about the physical and social world, and language.
courses.prerequisites: PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V or HDE 100B or HDE 100A or HDE 100AV.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have taken HDE 101.

courses.title: Social & Personality Development
courses.description: Social and personality development of children, infancy through adolescence. Topics include the development of personality, achievement motivation, self-understanding, sex-role identity, and antisocial behavior. Emphasis on the interface between biological and social factors.
courses.prerequisites: PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V or HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B or HDE 100BV.

courses.title: Infant Development
courses.description: Psychological development in infancy. Topics include physical and motor development, sensory and nervous system development, and memory and cognitive development. Emphasis will be on evaluating theories, empirical research, and experimental methods for understanding infant development.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V or HDE 100A or HDE 100AV).

courses.title: Developmental Cognitive Neuroscience
courses.description: Neuroscientific theories and methods (EEG, ERP, fNIRS, fMRI) that inform an understanding of behavioral and cognitive development over infancy and childhood. Neurodevelopmental correlates of perception, action, language, and social cognition; value of the neuroscientific perspective; limitations and challenges of neuroscientific research in the developmental context.
courses.prerequisites: PSC 135 or ((PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V or HDE 100A or HDE 100B); (PSC 101 or PSC 121 or NPB 161 or HDE 163));PSC 141 recommended.

courses.title: The Development of Memory
courses.description: Theory and research on memory development with focus on infancy and childhood.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V or PSC 141 or PSC 142 or PSC 100 or PSC 130).
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed former PSC 133.

courses.title: Developmental Disorders
courses.description: Current scientific knowledge of the influences of biological, cognitive, and environmental factors on the emergence of disorders with onset in childhood. Examples include autism spectrum, ADD/ADHD, dyslexia and dyscalculia. Emphasis placed on understanding these disorders, their causes and their treatments.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V or PSC 141 or HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B or HDE 100BV).

courses.title: Relationship Science: Lust, Love, & Evolution
courses.description: Evolutionary perspectives on attraction and close relationships. Integrating social psychological and evolutionary theories with empirical evidence pertaining to human mating.
courses.prerequisites: PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V;PSC 041 recommended.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 051.

courses.title: Relationship Science: Lust, Love, & Evolution
courses.description: Evolutionary perspectives on attraction and close relationships. Integrating social psychological and evolutionary theories with empirical evidence pertaining to human mating.
courses.prerequisites: PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V;PSC 041 recommended.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 051.

courses.title: Social Psychology
courses.description: Behavior of the individual in the group. Examination of basic psychological processes in social situations, surveying various problems of social interaction: group tensions, norm-development, attitudes, values, public opinion, status.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed former PSC 145.

courses.title: Social Psychology
courses.description: Behavior of the individual in the group. Examination of basic psychological processes in social situations, surveying various problems of social interaction: group tensions, norm-development, attitudes, values, public opinion, status.
courses.activities: Web Virtual Lecture 3 hour(s), Web Electronic Discussion 1 hour(s).
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed former PSC 145.

courses.title: Social Cognition
courses.description: Examines how social factors influence how we attend to, encode, and process information and how these mental processes affect subsequent judgments and behavior.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

courses.title: Psychology & Law
courses.description: Current theoretical and empirical issues in the study of psychology and law. Topics include eyewitness testimony, child abuse, jury decision making, juvenile delinquency and criminology, prediction of violence, insanity defense, and memory for traumatic events.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed former PSC 115.

courses.title: Psychology of Emotion
courses.description: Introduction to current theories and research on emotion and bodily feelings with special reference to self-knowledge.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

courses.title: Psychology of Emotion
courses.description: Introduction to current theories and research on emotion and bodily feelings with special reference to self-knowledge.
courses.activities: Web Virtual Lecture 3 hour(s), Web Electronic Discussion 1 hour(s).

courses.title: The Psychology of Cultural Appropriation
courses.description: Social psychological approach to study of cultural appropriation; integration of social psychological theories with empirical evidence and examples from popular press and digital media; development of critical and integrative ways of thinking about theory and research on intergroup relations, identity, and social inequality; examines routes to cultural appreciation.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

courses.title: The Psychology of Diversity in Aging
courses.description: Psychological perspectives on various parameters of diversity in aging and older adulthood to explore cross-cultural differences, aging assumptions, ageism, discrimination, and resilience. Optimal aging, generativity, Indigenous healthy brain aging, LGBTQIA2S+ health. Disparities in cognitive functioning, health, and longevity. Evaluation of gerontological theories, methodologies, and current empirical research.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V); or consent of instructor.
courses.creditLimitations: Only two units of credit to students who have taken HDE 100C.

courses.title: Stereotyping, Prejudice, & Stigma
courses.description: Social psychological underpinnings of stereotyping, prejudice, and stigma from sociocultural, motivational, and cognitive perspectives. Topics include: origins, maintenance, change, effects on person perception and memory, and the automaticity/controllability of stereotyping and prejudice.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

courses.title: Sexual Orientation & Prejudice
courses.description: Current scientific knowledge about sexual orientation and prejudice based on sexual orientation. Emphasis is placed on learning the skills necessary for a critical understanding of science and public policy issues relevant to sexuality.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).
courses.ge: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH); Domestic Diversity (DD); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Gender & Human Reproduction
courses.description: Psychology of reproduction. Reproductive events over the course of an individualâs life, including sexual development, mate choice, relationships, and reproduction. Biological and social psychological explanations at the levels of mechanism and evolutionary function.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed former PSC 149. (Former PSC 149.)

courses.title: Psychology of the Self
courses.description: Psychological theory and research on the self. Topics include: self-knowledge, self-esteem, self-regulation, self-presentation, cognitive and emotional aspects of the self, and the role of the self in shaping social interaction.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

courses.title: Introduction to Personality Psychology
courses.description: Scientific study of personality. Methods of personality research. Overview of current research and theory in the field of personality psychology.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed former PSC 147.

courses.title: Introduction to Clinical Psychology
courses.description: Major theoretical formulations in the history of clinical psychology, from classical psychoanalysis to contemporary existentialism and behavior modification. Survey based on lectures, films, and tapes, of what clinical psychologists do, including methods of appraisal, professional roles, and approaches to treatment.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

courses.title: Mental Health, Mental Illness, & Problems in Living
courses.description: Overview of psychological disorders and psychological conditions that lead to problems in daily living, with consideration of causes, classification systems, and treatment.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

courses.title: The Science of Multi-Cultural Psychology
courses.description: Effects of culture and ethnicity on psychological processes, such as social cognition, emotion, motivation, personality, self-concept, and interpersonal behavior (i.e., how culture makes who you are). Individuals' construction of multicultural identity and experiences.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

courses.title: Psychology of Religion
courses.description: Major theories, issues, data, and research methodologies of the psychology of religion. Religious experience and expression; religious development in childhood, adolescence, and adulthood; conversion; religious influences on physical and mental health; cross-cultural perspectives.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

courses.title: Genius, Creativity, & Leadership
courses.description: Phenomenon of genius is examined from a diversity of theoretical, methodological, and disciplinary perspectives, with an emphasis on outstanding creativity and leadership in art, music, literature, philosophy, science, war, and politics.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); or equivalents, or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Research in Cognitive & Perceptual Psychology
courses.description: Empirical research on selected topics in general experimental psychology (general research design and analysis, perception, cognition, cognitive development, etc.). Specific content will vary from quarter to quarter.
courses.prerequisites: PSC 041 or PSC 041V; four upper division Psychology courses and consent of instructor.

courses.title: Research in Psychobiology
courses.description: Empirical research on selected topics in psychobiology (animal learning, animal behavior, physiological and sensory psychology, developmental psychobiology, computer modeling of neural systems). Content varies.
courses.prerequisites: PSC 101; three additional upper division Psychology courses and consent of instructor.

courses.title: Research in Personality & Social Psychology
courses.description: Empirical research on selected topics in personality and social psychology (personality, social psychology, organizational psychology, etc.). Content will vary from quarter to quarter.
courses.prerequisites: PSC 041 or PSC 041V; four upper division Psychology courses and consent of instructor.

courses.title: Research in Developmental Psychology
courses.description: Empirical research on selected topics in developmental psychology (research design and analysis, development, cognitive development, social and personality development etc.).
courses.prerequisites: PSC 041 or PSC 041V; consent of instructor; Four upper division Psychology courses.

courses.title: Methods in Laboratory Research
courses.description: Training in specific lab-based research methods coupled with hands-on experience in a research lab. Students assessed on their ability report and interpret research findings. Content varies from quarter to quarter.

courses.title: History of Psychology
courses.description: Development of psychological thought and research in context of history of philosophy and science.
courses.prerequisites: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); upper division standing or consent of instructor.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 120. (Former PSC 120.)

courses.title: Seminar in Psychology
courses.description: Intensive treatment of a special topic or problem of psychological interest.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; major in Psychology or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Upper Division Seminar
courses.description: In-depth examination at an upper division level of a special topic in Psychology. Emphasis on student participation in learning. May not be repeated for credit.
courses.prerequisites: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

courses.title: Fieldwork in Psychology
courses.description: Supervised internship off and on campus, in community and institutional settings. Maximum of 6 units may be used towards satisfaction of upper division major requirement.
courses.prerequisites: Consent of instructor; upper division standing in Psychology.

courses.title: Tutoring in Psychology
courses.description: Intended for advanced undergraduate students who will lead discussion sections in Psychology courses.
courses.prerequisites: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

courses.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

courses.title: Proseminar in Psychology
courses.description: Introduces matriculating graduate students to research activities of departmental faculty.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Research Preceptorship
courses.description: Research preceptorship.

courses.title: Research Seminar
courses.description: Presentation of graduate research to program faculty and graduate students.

courses.title: Data Cleaning & Management in the Social Sciences
courses.description: Theoretical and technical skills to build a data cleaning and management pipeline. Programming in R, applied data analysis, workflow, and data documentation.

courses.title: Data Visualization in the Social Sciences
courses.description: Conceptual and technical skills to build data effective, evidence-based figures and graphics for the social sciences using the R programming language. Basic programming for data visualization; R programming language; ggplot2; cognitive approaches to data visualization; frequency distributions; visualizing associations; visualizing uncertainty; piecing plots together; building interactive visualizations.
courses.prerequisites: PSC 203AB or better; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Statistical Analysis of Psychological Experiments
courses.description: Probability theory, sampling distributions, statistical inference, and hypothesis testing using standard parametric and correlational approaches. Analysis of variance, factorial and repeated measures, and tests of trends.
courses.prerequisites: STA 102; or equivalent; graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 206.

courses.title: Causal Modeling of Correlational Data
courses.description: Examination of how to make causal inferences from correlational data in the behavioral sciences. Emphasis is on testing rival causal models using correlations among observed variables. Beginning with multiple regression analysis, discussion advances to path analysis and related techniques.
courses.prerequisites: PSC 204A; or the equivalent course and graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 207A.

courses.title: Advanced Statistical Inference from Psychological Experiments
courses.description: Advanced topics in statistical inference, which may include probability theory, sampling distributions, statistical inference and hypothesis testing, nonparametric statistics, Bayesian approaches, and advanced issues in analysis of variance.
courses.prerequisites: PSC 204A; or the equivalent; graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 205.

courses.title: Applied Multivariate Analysis of Psychological Data
courses.description: Review of the major methods of multivariate data analysis for psychological data. Students will program statistical routines using a linear algebra-based computing language. Topics will include multivariate analysis of variance. discriminant analysis, canonical analysis factor analysis, and component analysis.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 207B. (Former PSC 207B.)

courses.title: Factor Analysis
courses.description: Theory and methods of factor analysis, including exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, and principal component analysis.
courses.prerequisites: PSC 204A;PSC 204B; or equivalent courses, or consent of instructor; graduate standing.

courses.title: Structural Equation Modeling
courses.description: Theory and methods of structural equation modeling, including path analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, multiple-group modeling and latent growth curve modeling.
courses.prerequisites: PSC 204A;PSC 204B; or equivalent courses, or consent of instructor; graduate standing.

courses.title: Multilevel Models
courses.description: Introduction to statistical techniques for the analysis of normal, hierarchically structured data, such as cross-sectional clustered data or repeated-measures data. Topics include hierarchical linear models, latent growth curve models, and how these methods handle unbalanced and/or missing data.
courses.prerequisites: PSC 204A; graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Applied Psychometrics & Measurement Theory
courses.description: Examination of the basic principles and applications of classical and modern test theory. Topics include test construction, reliability theory, validity theory, factor analysis, and latent trait theory.
courses.prerequisites: PSC 204A; graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 204 or PSC 204C.

courses.title: Item Response Theory
courses.description: Item response theory allows for the creation of precise measurement instruments in psychological testing. Review Classical Test Theory, and then cover basic IRT models through advanced applications.
courses.prerequisites: PSC 204A; or the equivalent; graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Applied Longitudinal Data Analysis
courses.description: Modeling and understanding of intraindividual change and interindividual differences in change. Reviews conventional methods and introduces contemporary techniques for modeling intraindividual change.
courses.prerequisites: PSC 204A; graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Applied Bayesian Statistics for Social Scientists
courses.description: Bayesian methodology and inference for social scientists. Basics of probability theory, Bayes' theorem, inference and model checking, discussion of common distributions, sampling approaches, Bayes factors for hypothesis testing and introduction to dedicated software.

courses.title: Theoretical Foundations: Research Methods in Psychology
courses.description: Examines the philosophy and research practices underlying experimental psychology. Topics to be covered include philosophy of science/epistemology, research design, inference and bias in research, theory development, validity, the social context of research, and critical thinking about research.

courses.title: Research Methods in Psychology: Applications in Social-Personality Research
courses.description: Overview of the research designs, assessment methods, and statistical procedure used by social-personality psychologists. Focus on the practical issues that arise when using each method in specific research contexts.

courses.title: Survey & Questionnaire Research Methods
courses.description: Survey and questionnaire research methods with emphasis on how to ask questions. Cognitive, motivational, and social processes that influence how respondents answer questions; sampling techniques; Internet resources; practical aspects of fielding survey and questionnaire research.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of a course on social or behavioral research methods; graduate standing.

courses.title: Physiological Psychology
courses.description: A conceptual analysis of the contributions of neuroanatomy, neurophysiology and neurochemistry to an understanding of animal and human behavior.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Human Electrophysiology
courses.description: In-depth introduction and hands-on experience with the event-related potential (ERP) method in the study of attention, executive control, memory, language and social cognitive neuroscience.
courses.activities: Lecture/Discussion 1.50 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s), Extensive Problem Solving 1.50 hour(s), Project (Term Project) 3 hour(s).

courses.title: Introduction to Programming: Matlab
courses.description: The Matlab programming environment as a means of organizing, analyzing, and visualizing scientific data. Basic programming concepts such as variables, loops, conditional branching, and efficient programming techniques will be emphasized.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Cognitive Neuroimaging
courses.description: Introduction to empirical foundations and methodology of neuroimaging, emphasizing pragmatics of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to study cognition. Topics include MR physics, the relationship between neural activity and the BOLD response, experimental design, and analysis of fMRI data.
courses.prerequisites: Basic knowledge of inferential statistics and experimental Psychology.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Neuroimaging
courses.description: Critical presentation and discussion of the most influential advanced issues in neuroimaging, emphasizing fMRI design/analysis and the integration of fMRI with EEG/MEG.

courses.title: Developmental Psychology: Cognitive & Perceptual Development
courses.description: Theories and empirical findings concerning human cognitive and perceptual development. Development of perception, memory, concepts (e.g., theory of mind, concepts about number), problem solving, and language from infancy to adolescence.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor; completion of an undergraduate or graduate course on developmental psychology or human development.

courses.title: Developmental Psychology: Social, Emotional, & Personality Development
courses.description: Theories and empirical findings concerning human social, emotional, and personality development. Development of emotions, moral reasoning and behavior, personality, self-concept, and social cognition from infancy to adolescence (may include adulthood).
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor; completion of an undergraduate or graduate course on developmental psychology or human development.

courses.title: Developmental Cognitive Neuroscience
courses.description: Introduction to theories and methods, such as EEG, fNIRS, and fMRI, that inform cognitive development in infants and children. Classic and cutting-edge articles illustrate the value and challenges of using developmental cognitive neuroscience to study perception, action, language, and social cognition.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor; completion of an undergraduate or graduate course on any of the following topics: developmental psychology, human development, neuroscience, cognitive neuroscience.

courses.title: Behavioral Genetics
courses.description: Review basic principles in genetics and select topics in molecular genetics with emphasis on behavior. Use of modern molecular methods to outline complex relationships between genes, environment, and behavior.
courses.activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion/Laboratory 1 hour(s), Term Paper.
courses.creditLimitations: Not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 251.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Animal Behavior
courses.description: Survey of the phenomena and theory of animal behavior from the perspectives of multiple biological disciplines, including evolution, ecology, psychology, genetics, neurobiology, endocrinology, and animal science.
courses.prerequisites: Consent of instructor; upper division undergraduate introduction to the biology of behavior, such as PSC 101,PSC 122,PSC 123,NPB 102,NPB 150,NPB 152,WFC 141,ENT 104, or ANS 105.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Animal Behavior
courses.description: Survey of the phenomena and theory of animal behavior from the perspectives of multiple biological disciplines, including evolution, ecology, psychology, genetics, neurobiology, endocrinology, and animal science.

courses.title: History of Psychology
courses.description: A lecture-seminar on the history of psychology and on the applicability of early psychological theory and research to contemporary investigations.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Academic Writing in Psychology
courses.description: Strategies for developing and honing academic writing skills and writing productivity, with a particular focus on how to write a clear and compelling empirical journal article in psychology.

courses.title: Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: Analysis of the mental processes by which knowledge is acquired, manipulated, stored, retrieved and used.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Sensation & Perception
courses.description: Analysis of the role of sensory processes and perception in experience and their effects on behavior.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Attitudes & Social Influence
courses.description: Survey of theory and research in the field of attitudes and social influence. Topics include attitude definition and measurement, major theories of attitude formation and change, the relationship between attitudes and behavior, and recent directions and controversies.

courses.title: Attraction & Close Relationships
courses.description: Social psychological theory and research on attraction and close relationships, with a particular emphasis on romantic relationships. Covers attachment theory, interdependence theory, and evolutionary psychological perspectives.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Psychology, Sociology, Human Development, a related social science, or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Social Cognition
courses.description: Processes underlying the perception, memory, and judgment of social stimuli, the effects of social and affective factors on cognition, and the interpersonal consequences of those processes. Topics include automaticity/control, motivated cognition, person perception, stereotyping, attitudes, and persuasion.

courses.title: Stereotyping, Prejudice, & Stigma
courses.description: Examines the social psychological underpinnings of stereotyping, prejudice, and stigma, including sociocultural, motivational, and cognitive factors.

courses.title: Social Psychology
courses.description: Theory and research in social psychology.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Personality
courses.description: Theory and research in human personality.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Topics in Genetic Correlates of Behavior
courses.description: Theory and experiment in the genetic contributions to animal and human behavior.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Topics in Psychobiology
courses.description: Critical study in a selected area of psychobiology.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Cognitive Neuroscience
courses.description: Graduate core course for neuroscience. Neurobiological bases of higher mental function including attention, memory, language. One of three in three-quarter sequence.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate student standing in Psychology or Neuroscience or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Topics in Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: Selected topics in language processing, memory, perception, problem solving, and thinking, with an emphasis on the common underlying cognitive processes.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Topics in Psycholinguistics
courses.description: Discussion of fundamental issues in the psychology of language.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Topics in Personality & Social Psychology
courses.description: Critical study of a selected area of personality or social psychology.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate student standing or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Core Concepts & Methods in Learning, Memory, & Plasticity
courses.description: Core concepts and methods used in studies of learning, memory and plasticity. Behavioral paradigms and measurement approaches in human and animal studies of learning and plasticity, as well as a consideration of the functional, anatomical and neuronal mechanisms underlying brain plasticity.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Core Concepts & Methods in Learning, Memory, & Plasticity
courses.description: Core concepts and detailed survey methods used in studies of learning, memory and plasticity, from the cellular and molecular level to the level of neural circuits. Areas of learning, memory, and plasticity research where recent progress has been made in linking across these levels of analysis.

courses.title: Translational Approaches to Learning, Memory, & Plasticity Disorders
courses.description: Neurological disorders, the effect of these disorders on learning, memory and plasticity, approved therapeutic options and current research designed to improve understanding and treatment of these diseases: (i) the clinical presentation, diagnostic criteria, and existing therapies, (ii) mechanistic studies in humans and animal models, and (iii) molecular pathways involved in the disease and approaches for drug discovery.

courses.title: Topics in Developmental Psychology
